Implementation notes: this is a read-only query that selects from discussion_board_article_snapshots and may join discussion_board_articles to filter by article author; no write operations occur. The operation must respect the table's audit semantics: snapshots are append-only and preserved even if the original article is deleted. Use database indexes (snapshot_at, article id, trigram title/content) for performant queries.

It operates directly on the Prisma model discussion_board_article_snapshots which denormalizes article fields at snapshot time (title, content, state, snapshot_at, original created_at/updated_at and deleted_at). The snapshot table is append-only; snapshots persist independently of article lifecycle changes so audit history remains available even if the article is later modified or removed.

Security and permissions: access to snapshots contains historical content and audit data; only moderator actors should call this endpoint. The service expects caller authorization to be enforced by the controller layer and will surface snapshot content only to authorized actors.

Filtering and business logic: request parameters allow filtering by articleId, authorId (via the article relation), state (draft|published|pending_review|hidden), snapshot time ranges, and free-text search over title and content. Pagination and sorting parameters support standard page/limit and sort by snapshot_at, created_at, or relevance. The operation returns a paginated summary view (IPageIDiscussionBoardArticleSnapshot.ISummary) optimized for listing; the summary includes snapshot id, article id, snapshot_at, title excerpt, state and minimal audit timestamps.

Error handling and expected behavior: invalid filters (malformed UUIDs or invalid enums) return 400. When query results are large, the implementation should use DB indexes described in the Prisma schema (Gin trigram indexes on title/content, snapshot_at index) to maintain performance.

This operation manipulates rows in the Prisma model `discussion_board_attachments` associated with a parent `discussion_board_articles` record. The implementation MUST enforce referential integrity (discussion_board_attachments.discussion_board_article_id -> discussion_board_articles.id), per-article attachment limits (max 5 attachments per article, max 3 image attachments), and per-file constraints (mime_type and size) as defined by product business rules. operations.description:
Purpose and overview:

Update the attachments associated with a specific article. This endpoint updates rows in the `discussion_board_attachments` table by creating new attachment records, associating existing temporary uploads to the article, removing associations, or reordering attachments. Each attachment row contains fields such as `storage_key`, `original_filename`, `mime_type`, `size` and `is_image` which are used to validate and render attachments.

Security and permissions:

Only authenticated members who are the article author or privileged moderator/administrator actors are allowed to perform this operation. The provider implementation MUST verify that the requester either (a) is the author of the article (discussion_board_articles.discussion_board_member_id) or (b) has a moderator role. All actions performed via this endpoint MUST be recorded in the application audit logs (e.g., event type `attachment.update.applied`) and any security-relevant side effects (malware scan failures) must be emitted to moderation/operational queues.

Relationship to underlying database entities:

This operation directly creates/updates/removes `discussion_board_attachments` rows that reference `discussion_board_articles.id` via `discussion_board_article_id`. Implementation MUST use foreign-key relations to ensure referential integrity and follow cascade semantics defined in the Prisma schema. Soft-delete semantics are represented by `deleted_at` on the attachment and/or parent article; the provider should honor `deleted_at` when deciding visibility or delete scheduling.

Validation rules and business logic:

- Enforce per-article attachment limits: at most 5 attachments attached to a single article, and at most 3 images among those attachments.
- Validate each attachment's `mime_type` and `size` against allowed lists and size limits. Reject the entire request (atomic behavior) if any attachment violates rules.
- When creating new attachment rows, ensure `storage_key` references a successfully persisted object in the file storage system and schedule or run a malware/abuse scan before marking the attachment available for public visibility.
- When removing attachments, schedule storage cleanup asynchronously and ensure retention/purge windows are honored via the data-lifecycle policy rather than performing immediate irreversible storage deletion in the synchronous request.

Related operations:

- POST /articles/{id}/attachments — companion upload endpoint to create temporary uploads or direct-stored objects referenced by `storage_key`.
- GET /articles/{articleId}/attachments/{attachmentId} — retrieve metadata for a single attachment after update to confirm state.

Expected behavior and error handling:

- Atomicity: either all requested changes succeed and the server returns the updated article (including the attachments array), or the request fails with an error and no changes are applied.
- Typical error responses: 400 for validation errors (exceeding attachment counts, invalid mime_type/size), 401 if unauthenticated, 403 if not author or moderator, 404 if article not found, 409 for storage-key conflicts, 500 for unexpected server errors.
- On success return the updated article with its attachments (response DTO `IDiscussionBoardArticle`), with attachments reflecting persisted database rows from `discussion_board_attachments`.

operations.description:
Purpose and overview:

Return attachment metadata for a specific article attachment. The response provides descriptive and operational fields (`original_filename`, `mime_type`, `size`, `is_image`, `storage_key`, `created_at`) sufficient for UI rendering, preview decisions and to request a download URL. This operation does not stream binary content; binary downloads are provided via a separate download endpoint or signed CDN URLs.

Security and visibility considerations:

This endpoint is read-only. For published articles and attachments it may be public; however, if the parent article's state is `hidden`, `pending_review` or the parent has a non-null `deleted_at`, the implementation MUST enforce access controls and return 404 or 403 according to product policy. Note: unlike comment-attachments, `discussion_board_attachments` does not have a `quarantined` boolean column in the current Prisma schema. If your product requires quarantining article attachments, that capability must be added to the schema or represented via a moderation artifact before this operation can depend on it.

Relationship to underlying DB entities:

Reads from `discussion_board_attachments` and validates the parent relation with `discussion_board_article_id`. The implementation must respect `deleted_at` on both the attachment and the parent article when determining accessibility.

Validation rules and error handling:

- Validate path parameters (UUID format). Return 400 if malformed.
- Return 404 if the article or attachment is not found, or if the attachment is not associated with the provided articleId.
- Return 403 if the article/attachment is not public and the requester lacks authorization.
- On success return the attachment DTO `IDiscussionBoardAttachment`; do not stream binary content in this response.

Related operations:

- GET /attachments/{id}/download or a signed-URL exchange endpoint for retrieving binary content.
- PATCH /articles/{articleId}/attachments (update) used to change attachment associations or metadata.

Expected behavior and error handling:

- Successful response: HTTP 200 with attachment metadata DTO.
- Errors: 400 for invalid UUIDs, 404 for missing resources or mismatched parent-child relationship, 403 for access denied, 500 for unexpected server errors.

operations.specification: This operation uploads one or more attachments for a target article and persists metadata to the discussion_board_attachments table in the Prisma schema. It is associated primarily with the discussion_board_attachments table (discussion_board_attachments) and references the parent article (discussion_board_articles.id) and optional uploading member (discussion_board_member.id). The implementation must persist attachment metadata fields present in the Prisma model: discussion_board_article_id, discussion_board_member_id, original_filename, storage_key, mime_type, size, is_image, created_at, deleted_at. The operation supports two upload patterns: (1) direct multipart/form-data uploads where the server stores the file and returns a storage_key, and (2) client-side direct upload using pre-signed URIs where the client provides a storage_key/uri in the request body. Business validation rules derived from the project requirements must be enforced: allowed mime types (images: image/jpeg, image/png, image/gif, image/webp; documents: application/pdf, text/plain, application/msword, application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document), per-file size limits (images <= 5 MB, documents <= 20 MB), per-article attachment limits (max 5 attachments per article) and image count limits (max 3 images per article). The operation should trigger asynchronous safety scanning (malware/abuse) and quarantine the attachment if scanning fails; quarantined attachments set a quarantine flag in the attachment metadata (implementation detail). The operation must create discussion_board_attachments rows and index them for article-based queries as defined in the Prisma schema. Storage object lifecycle (permanent deletion of stored file) is handled separately by purge/background workers after soft-delete; this API only persists metadata and returns created attachment metadata to the client.
operations.description:
Upload one or more attachments for a specific article.

Purpose and overview:
This endpoint accepts attachment uploads (images or document files) intended to be associated with the article identified by the path parameter articleId. It records metadata in the discussion_board_attachments table described in the Prisma schema (fields: id, discussion_board_article_id, discussion_board_member_id, original_filename, storage_key, mime_type, size, is_image, created_at, deleted_at). The operation supports either server-mediated multipart/form-data uploads or client-side direct uploads (pre-signed URI) where the request body includes the final storage_key. For multipart uploads the server returns storage_key values after persisting the file to object storage.

Security, permissions and actors:
Only authenticated members may call this endpoint. Authorization logic must verify that the caller is permitted to attach files to the target article: typically the article author or an authorized member session; moderators retain elevated privileges. The API requires authentication (JWT bearer) and should record the uploader's member id in discussion_board_member_id when available. The operation logs upload events into audit trails (discussion_board_audit_logs) and integrates with the asynchronous scanning/queuing systems described in the requirements.

Relationship to database entities and business rules:
This operation writes to discussion_board_attachments and links each attachment to discussion_board_articles via discussion_board_article_id. It must enforce the project's attachment business rules: allowed mime types, per-file size limits, and per-article attachment/count limits (max 5 attachments per article, max 3 images per article). If the article does not exist or is not in a state that accepts attachments (e.g., permanently deleted), the API must return 404 or 409 as appropriate.

Validation rules and expected behavior:
- Validate articleId exists (discussion_board_articles.id) and is not permanently purged.
- Enforce per-article attachment quotas; reject with 409 if adding requested files would exceed limits.
- Validate file mime types and file sizes (images ≤ 5 MB; documents ≤ 20 MB).
- Persist metadata to discussion_board_attachments and return created metadata objects. If scanning fails, mark the attachment as quarantined (implementation detail) and surface quarantine status in response. The uploaded file storage lifecycle (actual object deletion) is handled by background purge jobs; this endpoint only sets metadata and deleted_at when deletion is requested.

Related operations and error handling:
- Related: GET /articles/{articleId} to fetch article details and attachment lists; GET /attachments/{id} to fetch attachment metadata and download URIs; DELETE /articles/{articleId}/attachments/{attachmentId} to remove an attachment (soft-delete).
- Errors: 400 Bad Request for invalid inputs; 401 Unauthorized for unauthenticated requests; 403 Forbidden for insufficient privileges; 404 Not Found if articleId does not exist; 409 Conflict for quota exceed or concurrent upload conflicts; 413 Payload Too Large when single file exceeds server limits; 500 Internal Server Error for unexpected failures. The response includes clear messages matching the validation rules and references to allowed mime types and size limits.

operations.description:
Remove (soft-delete) an attachment associated with an article.

Purpose and overview:
This endpoint marks the specified attachment as deleted in the discussion_board_attachments table by setting the deleted_at timestamp, preserving the metadata for audit and retention windows. The operation does not, by itself, guarantee immediate removal of the object from object storage — storage cleanup is performed by background purge workflows that honor retention, quarantine and legal hold policies.

Security considerations and permissions:
Only authenticated members are allowed to invoke this endpoint. Business rules require that deletion is restricted to the attachment uploader, the parent article's author, or moderators/administrators. The endpoint should perform authorization checks accordingly. All moderator-initiated deletions must create corresponding moderation audit entries (discussion_board_moderation_actions and discussion_board_moderation_audit) per the moderation model.

Relationship to underlying DB entities and behavior:
This operation updates discussion_board_attachments.deleted_at for the row identified by attachmentId and ensures the row is still linked to the specified articleId. If the attachment is already soft-deleted, the API may return 404 Not Found or 204 No Content depending on design choice; the specification below assumes idempotent behavior (204 on repeated deletes). If the attachment does not belong to the specified article, return 400 or 409 to indicate mismatched context.

Validation rules and business logic:
- Verify articleId exists and that the attachment with attachmentId exists and its discussion_board_article_id matches the path articleId.
- Verify the caller is authorized (uploader, article author, or moderator). Unauthorized callers receive 403 Forbidden.
- Set deleted_at to current timestamp (soft-delete) and record an audit entry describing the deletion actor, reason and timing.
- Schedule storage cleanup per purge schedule; do not remove storage objects synchronously in this request.

Related operations and error handling:
- Related: POST /articles/{articleId}/attachments (upload attachments); GET /attachments/{id} (get metadata); GET /articles/{articleId} (list attachments); background purge worker for permanent deletion.
- Errors: 401 Unauthorized; 403 Forbidden; 404 Not Found if attachment or article not found; 409 Conflict if attachment is not associated with the article; 500 Internal Server Error for unexpected failures.

All moderator-initiated deletions must create corresponding moderation audit entries (discussion_board_moderation_actions and discussion_board_moderation_audit) per the moderation model.

Relationship to underlying DB entities and behavior:
This operation updates discussion_board_attachments.deleted_at for the row identified by attachmentId and ensures the row is still linked to the specified articleId. If the attachment is already soft-deleted, the API may return 404 Not Found or 204 No Content depending on design choice; the specification below assumes idempotent behavior (204 on repeated deletes). If the attachment does not belong to the specified article, return 400 or 409 to indicate mismatched context.

Validation rules and business logic:
- Verify articleId exists and that the attachment with attachmentId exists and its discussion_board_article_id matches the path articleId.
- Verify the caller is authorized (uploader, article author, or moderator). Unauthorized callers receive 403 Forbidden.
- Set deleted_at to current timestamp (soft-delete) and record an audit entry describing the deletion actor, reason and timing.
- Schedule storage cleanup per purge schedule; do not remove storage objects synchronously in this request.

Related operations and error handling:
- Related: POST /articles/{articleId}/attachments (upload attachments); GET /attachments/{id} (get metadata); GET /articles/{articleId} (list attachments); background purge worker for permanent deletion.
- Errors: 401 Unauthorized; 403 Forbidden; 404 Not Found if attachment or article not found; 409 Conflict if attachment is not associated with the article; 500 Internal Server Error for unexpected failures.

Implementation notes: the provider must apply filters (author id, parentCommentId, isHidden, text search over content) and support pagination, sorting (created_at desc by default), and optional threading flattening. Deleted comments (where deleted_at IS NOT NULL) must be excluded from public results. The operation should also consider moderation state: comments with is_hidden = true are excluded from public listings unless the requesting actor is a moderator. Response uses summary DTOs and paginated envelope to optimize list rendering.
operations.description:
Purpose and overview:

Retrieve a filtered, sorted and paginated list of comments that belong to a single article. This operation is intended for article comment listings and supports search (full-text/trigram on content), filtering by author, parent comment, moderation state, and pagination. Results are returned in a paginated envelope containing comment summary items to minimize payload size.

Security considerations and user permissions:

This is a public read operation for standard audiences. However, comments that are soft-deleted (discussion_board_comments.deleted_at IS NOT NULL) or explicitly hidden by moderation (is_hidden = true) MUST NOT be returned to unauthenticated or non-moderator actors. Authorization checks and additional fields returned must be implemented in the business layer; the public API surface is unauthenticated ([]). Moderator actors will require a separate authenticated endpoint or an actor-aware variant to include hidden comments.

Relationship to underlying database entities:

This operation maps to the discussion_board_comments table in the Prisma schema. Key columns used: discussion_board_article_id (scoping), content (search), discussion_board_author_id (author filtering), discussion_board_parent_comment_id (threading), is_hidden (moderation filtering), created_at/updated_at (sorting and pagination) and deleted_at (soft-delete filtering). The endpoint must join or hydrate author summary information from discussion_board_member as necessary for the response DTO.

Validation rules and business logic:

- articleId path parameter must be a UUID corresponding to an existing discussion_board_articles.id; if article not found, return 404.
- Request body (IDiscussionBoardComment.IRequest) provides pagination (page, limit), optional search string (search), optional filters (authorId, parentCommentId, includeThreaded boolean), and sorting instructions (sort = createdAt or -createdAt). Default sorting is created_at desc. Page/limit defaults must be applied server-side and limited to sensible maxima.
- Comments with deleted_at != NULL are excluded from results. Comments with is_hidden = true are excluded for public callers.

Related API operations:

- GET /articles/{articleId}/comments/{commentId} — retrieve a single comment detail (useful for deep linking or comment permalinks).
- POST /articles/{articleId}/comments — create a new comment (writes into discussion_board_comments).
- PATCH /articles/{articleId}/comments — this search/list operation pairs with create/update endpoints for comment workflows.

Expected behavior and error handling:

- On malformed UUIDs or invalid request schemas, return 400 with validation details.
- On non-existent articleId, return 404.
- If filtering or search yields no results, return an empty data array with pagination metadata.
- If moderation service or search index is degraded, return either degraded results with a clear warning in response metadata or a 503 when listing cannot be safely served.

Purpose and overview:

Retrieve a single comment by its identifier within the context of a parent article. This endpoint provides full comment details suitable for permalinks, deep-linking, and client-side navigation to a specific comment. The returned structure includes author summary (from discussion_board_member), parent comment reference if present, content, timestamps, and moderation state.

Security considerations and user permissions:

This endpoint is public for standard, non-hidden comments. If the requested comment is hidden (is_hidden = true) or soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NOT NULL), the API must not disclose the content to unauthenticated or non-moderator callers; instead return 404 or 403 depending on policy. Moderator and admin callers may receive additional moderation metadata and history via separate authenticated endpoints.

Relationship to underlying database entities:

The primary source is discussion_board_comments. The operation validates that discussion_board_comments.discussion_board_article_id = {articleId} and that the comment's id matches commentId. It may join discussion_board_member to populate author summary fields. Fields of interest: id, discussion_board_article_id, discussion_board_author_id, discussion_board_parent_comment_id, content, is_hidden, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at.

Validation rules and business logic:

- Both articleId and commentId path parameters must be UUIDs. If either is malformed, return 400.
- If no comment exists with the given commentId scoped to the articleId (or the comment is soft-deleted/hidden for public), return 404.
- The API should include parent comment id (if present) to allow the client to render threading or provide a link back to the parent. Author public summary (id, username, displayName) should be included but personally identifiable fields like email must never be returned in this public endpoint.

Related API operations and usage:

- PATCH /articles/{articleId}/comments — search and list comments for an article.
- POST /articles/{articleId}/comments — create a new comment (used to link to newly-created comment detail). 

Expected behavior and error handling:

- On success return the full IDiscussionBoardComment object.
- On unauthorized attempts to view hidden content, return 403 when caller is authenticated but lacks moderator privileges; return 404 for public callers to avoid revealing the existence of moderated content.
- For system or DB errors return 500 with diagnostic correlation id for support.

The DB fields used are: discussion_board_article_id (FK), discussion_board_author_id (caller member id), discussion_board_parent_comment_id (nullable FK), content, is_hidden, created_at and updated_at timestamps. An optional parent comment id may be supplied to create a reply; when provided the API MUST validate that the parent exists, belongs to the same article, and that the resulting reply depth does not exceed the product policy maximum (application-enforced). Content length validation (per product policy; e.g., up to 500–5000 chars) and rate-limiting/anti-abuse checks MUST be enforced before persisting.

Security and moderation:
Only authenticated members (authorization actor: member) may create comments. The service MUST ensure the member is verified and not suspended before accepting the comment. Comments that trigger automated abuse heuristics should be routed to moderation: they may be persisted with is_hidden=true or flagged for review as determined by product policy. This operation does not allow clients to set moderation-only fields (is_hidden, deleted_at) directly.

DB relationships and error handling:

If articleId does not exist or is not in a commentable state, return 404. If parentCommentId is provided but invalid or from a different article, return 400. Validation errors yield 400, authentication/authorization errors yield 401/403, and rate-limit violations yield 429.

operations.description:
Purpose and overview:
This endpoint performs a recoverable deletion (soft-delete) of a comment stored in the `discussion_board_comments` table. The Prisma model defines a nullable `deleted_at` timestamp; therefore this operation sets `deleted_at` to the current UTC time instead of permanently removing the database row. Child comments and attachments are preserved and handled by application-level retention logic.

Security considerations and permissions:
Only authenticated actors may call this endpoint. The operation permits deletion when the caller is the original comment author (ownership) or an authorized moderator/administrator. The server MUST validate the authenticated actor's identity and role and must not allow unauthorized deletions. Moderator-initiated removals MUST create corresponding moderation audit records in `discussion_board_moderation_audit` and optionally a `discussion_board_moderation_actions` entry.

Relationship to DB entities:
This operation updates the `deleted_at` column of `discussion_board_comments`. It MUST validate that `commentId` exists and that it belongs to the provided `articleId` to avoid cross-article mismatches.

Validation and business rules:
- Validate `articleId` and `commentId` are valid UUIDs and that the comment belongs to the article; return 404 if not found or mismatched.
- Verify caller is the comment author or a moderator/admin; return 403 if not authorized.
- Check for active legal holds or appeals that prevent deletion; if present return 409 Conflict or 422 per policy.
- Set `deleted_at` to current UTC timestamp and record the actor and reason for audit.

Errors and related operations:
- 404 Not Found (invalid article/comment or mismatch)
- 403 Forbidden (insufficient permissions)
- 409 Conflict / 422 Unprocessable Entity (legal hold or active appeal)
- 500 Internal Server Error for unexpected failures

Purpose and overview:
This operation creates or updates `discussion_board_comment_attachments` records for the given comment. Clients MUST upload binary files to object storage first and provide `storage_key` URIs here. The API validates each manifest entry and creates metadata rows linking the attachment to `discussion_board_comment_id`.

Security and permissions:
Only authenticated members may add attachments. The caller must be the comment author or an authorized moderator to modify attachments. The server MUST set `discussion_board_uploaded_by_id` to the authenticated member id when available and MUST log creation events for audit.

Validation rules and business logic:
- Validate `articleId` and `commentId` exist and are correctly associated; return 404 if not.
- Enforce a per-comment attachment quota (MVP: max 1 attachment per comment) and return 400 when the quota would be exceeded.
- Each manifest entry must include: `storage_key` (string, required), `original_filename` (string), `mime_type` (string), and `size` (integer bytes). The server should validate `size` against configured limits and `mime_type` against allowed types.
- If integrated scanning flags a file, set `quarantined = true` and create a moderator review task; quarantined attachments must not be publicly served until cleared.

Response and error handling:
- On success return a paginated summary of the comment's attachments so clients can refresh the attachment list (IPageIDiscussionBoardCommentAttachment.ISummary).
- Errors: 400 Bad Request (validation errors or quota exceeded), 403 Forbidden (not allowed), 404 Not Found (article/comment mismatch), 422 Unprocessable Entity (storage_key unresolved or quarantined), 500 Internal Server Error for unexpected failures.

Purpose and overview:
This endpoint creates `discussion_board_comment_attachments` records that link previously uploaded storage objects to the specified comment. Clients MUST perform object uploads ahead-of-time to object storage and provide `storage_key` references in the manifest. The API will validate each manifest entry, create metadata rows and return the created attachment summaries.

Security and permissions:
Only authenticated members may add attachments to their own comments; moderators are also permitted to add or manage attachments. The server MUST assert author ownership or moderator role before creating attachments. All creation events MUST be logged for audit.

Validation rules and business logic:
- Validate `articleId` and `commentId` exist and are associated; return 404 for mismatches.
- Enforce per-comment attachment quota (MVP: max 1 attachment per comment). Quota enforcement MUST be atomic in a DB transaction.
- Request manifest items MUST include: `storage_key` (string, required), `original_filename` (string), `mime_type` (string), and `size` (integer bytes). The server MUST validate `size` and `mime_type` against configured limits.
- If integrated scanning flags a file, set `quarantined = true`, do not return a publicUrl, and create a moderator review task.
- The request body MUST NOT duplicate the path `commentId` or `articleId` fields (these are supplied in path parameters).

Response and error handling:
- On success return a paginated summary of the comment's attachments (IDs, original_filename, mime_type, size, is_image, quarantined, publicUrl) so clients can refresh the attachment list. Do NOT return raw internal `storage_key` in public responses.
- Errors: 400 Bad Request (validation errors or quota exceeded), 403 Forbidden (not allowed), 404 Not Found (article/comment mismatch), 422 Unprocessable Entity (storage_key unresolved or quarantined), 500 Internal Server Error for unexpected failures.

operations.summary: Permanently delete a comment attachment (discussion_board_comment_attachments)
operations.description:
Purpose and overview:
This operation permanently deletes a specific attachment that belongs to a comment on a specified article. It targets the discussion_board_comment_attachments table (fields: id, discussion_board_comment_id, discussion_board_uploaded_by_id, original_filename, storage_key, mime_type, size, is_image, quarantined, created_at). The operation verifies the hierarchical relationship article -> comment -> attachment before deletion.

Security considerations and user permissions:
Only authenticated members may call this endpoint. The server-side implementation MUST enforce that the caller is either the attachment uploader, the author of the parent article, or a moderator with appropriate privileges. All deletion actions MUST generate an immutable audit entry (discussion_board_moderation_audit and/or discussion_board_audit_logs) capturing actor id, action_type, event_payload (including storage_key), and timestamps.

Relationship to underlying database entities:
This operation checks discussion_board_articles (articleId) -> discussion_board_comments (commentId) -> discussion_board_comment_attachments (attachmentId). If the attachment's discussion_board_comment_id does not match commentId, or the comment's discussion_board_article_id does not match articleId, the implementation MUST return 404 Not Found.

Validation and business logic:
- Validate articleId, commentId and attachmentId as UUIDs and existence.
- Confirm hierarchical relation (article -> comment -> attachment); return 404 if inconsistent.
- Confirm caller authorization (uploader, article author, or moderator); return 403 when unauthorized.
- If attachment.quarantined is true, include quarantine metadata in the audit payload.
- Perform DB deletion and storage object removal in a transactional or compensating manner; if storage deletion fails, roll back DB deletion or persist a complete audit record including storage_key to enable forensic action.

Expected behavior and errors:
- Success: HTTP 204 No Content and an audit entry recorded.
- Not found: HTTP 404 when identifiers are missing or relation mismatch.
- Forbidden: HTTP 403 when caller lacks permission.
- Storage error: HTTP 500 with operational alert when storage deletion fails after retries.

operations.description:
Purpose and overview:
This operation updates tag assignments for a single article. It is backed by the discussion_board_article_tags junction table which enforces uniqueness on (discussion_board_article_id, discussion_board_tag_id). The endpoint accepts either a replacement list of tagIds or an action-based payload (e.g., { add: [tagId], remove: [tagId] }). Implementation MUST be atomic from the user's perspective: either the complete update succeeds or no change is applied.

Security and permissions:
Only authenticated members may call this endpoint. Business rules normally restrict tag management to the article author and moderators/administrators; the implementation MUST verify the caller's permission and record changes in the moderation/audit tables (discussion_board_moderation_audit or discussion_board_audit_logs).

Relationship to underlying database entities:
This operation references discussion_board_articles (articleId), discussion_board_tags (tag ids), and discussion_board_article_tags (junction table). The service MUST validate tag existence and active status where business rules require it.

Validation rules and business logic:
- Validate articleId as UUID and that the article exists; return 404 if not found.
- Validate each supplied tagId exists in discussion_board_tags; return 400 for invalid ids.
- Enforce per-article tag limit (business example: max 10 tags); return 400 when exceeded.
- Maintain atomicity: perform minimal set of insertions/deletions in a transaction.
- Respect DB unique constraint; return 409 when concurrent modifications cause constraint violations.
- Concurrency control: because this mutates state on a PATCH endpoint (exception to search semantics), implement optimistic concurrency (ETag/If-Match or article version token) or application-level locking to prevent lost updates.

Expected behavior and error handling:
- Success: HTTP 200 with the updated list of tag assignments (summary view).
- Validation error: HTTP 400 for invalid tag ids or tag limit exceeded.
- Forbidden: HTTP 403 if caller lacks permission.
- Not found: HTTP 404 if the article does not exist.
- Conflict: HTTP 409 if concurrent modifications produce constraint violations; clients should retry with current state.

If a supplied tag slug does not exist, creating it via this operation satisfies the dependency; failure to have the tag will cause validation errors.

The target article must exist before its tag assignments can be updated. POST /discussionBoard/member/articles creates the discussion_board_articles row and yields the articleId referenced by this PATCH; without an existing article the update will return 404.

operations.specification: Creates a tag assignment linking an existing Tag to an Article by inserting a row into the Prisma table discussion_board_article_tags. This operation maps directly to the discussion_board_article_tags table in the Prisma schema and must respect the table's composite uniqueness constraint @@unique([discussion_board_article_id, discussion_board_tag_id]). Clients SHOULD provide tagSlug (string) which the service will resolve to discussion_board_tags.id (discussion_board_tags has @@unique([slug])). The service MUST validate that the Article exists and is not soft-deleted (discussion_board_articles.deleted_at IS NULL). created_by_member_id MUST be derived from the authenticated member and MUST NOT be accepted from the client. Duplicate assignments must result in 409 Conflict. See description for validation rules and error handling.

operations.description:
Purpose and overview:

This endpoint assigns an existing tag to an article by creating a new discussion_board_article_tags row in the database. It enforces referential integrity and the junction table's composite uniqueness constraint. The API accepts the article identifier in the path and the tag identifier (by slug) in the request body; created_by_member_id and created_at are set by the service.

parameters.name: articleId
parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the target article

responseBody.description: Created article-tag assignment record

operations.name: create

prerequisites.description: Tag records must exist before they can be assigned to an article. POST /discussionBoard/moderator/tags creates discussion_board_tags rows (ensuring slug/name uniqueness and providing the tag id required by the assignment). If a supplied tag slug does not exist, creating it via this operation satisfies the dependency; failure to have the tag will cause validation errors.

The article must exist before a tag assignment row can be created. POST /discussionBoard/member/articles creates the discussion_board_articles record referenced by articleId; creating the article first ensures the assignment does not fail with 404 or FK constraint errors.

operations.specification: Deletes an existing tag assignment between a Tag and an Article by removing the corresponding row from the Prisma table discussion_board_article_tags. The junction model has no deleted_at column, so this operation performs a hard delete on the association row. The operation resolves tagSlug → tagId (discussion_board_tags.slug is globally unique), verifies the article exists and is not soft-deleted, verifies the association exists, and then deletes it. Application logic must verify the requesting member has permission to remove tags from the article (owner or moderator/admin). Consider creating an audit entry for moderator-driven removals.
operations.summary: Remove an existing tag assignment from an article (hard delete of discussion_board_article_tags row)
operations.description:
Purpose and overview:

Remove the association linking a discussion_board_tag to a discussion_board_article by deleting the matching discussion_board_article_tags row. This is a destructive operation (hard delete) because the junction model does not have a deleted_at column.

Security and permissions:

Requires an authenticated member. The service MUST validate that the requester is authorized to remove tags from the target article (author or moderator/admin). If not authorized, return 403.

Behavior and validation rules:

- Resolve tagSlug (path) to discussion_board_tags.id using the tag table's @@unique([slug]) constraint; if tag not found, return 404.
- Validate the article exists and is not soft-deleted (discussion_board_articles.deleted_at IS NULL); if not found or deleted, return 404.
- Verify an association row exists in discussion_board_article_tags for the resolved tag id and articleId; if not present return 404.
- Perform a hard delete of the association row. Application logic should record an audit entry for moderator actions if required by policy.

Errors:

- 204 No Content on success
- 400 Bad Request for malformed articleId or tagSlug
- 401 Unauthorized for unauthenticated requests
- 403 Forbidden if requester lacks permission
- 404 Not Found if article, tag, or association does not exist
- 500 Internal Server Error for unexpected failures

The target article (articleId) must exist and be active (not soft-deleted) before tag-assignment deletion. POST /discussionBoard/member/articles creates the article (provides discussion_board_articles.id) required to locate and validate the existing junction row.

operations.specification: Create a new report record in the discussion_board_reports Prisma table. This operation maps to the discussion_board_reports model and persists a member-submitted report about a polymorphic target (article, comment, attachment). It persists reporter_member_id (derived from the authenticated principal), optional reporter_session_id, target_type, target_id, reason_category and optional explanation. The Prisma schema enforces a unique constraint to prevent duplicate reports from the same reporter for the same target (reporter_member_id + target_type + target_id).
operations.summary: Create a content report submitted by an authenticated member (discussion_board_reports)
operations.description:
Allows an authenticated member to file a structured report against a content target (article, comment, attachment). The report is persisted into discussion_board_reports and subsequently processed by moderator workflows. The server MUST derive reporter_member_id from the authenticated principal and MUST NOT accept an arbitrary reporter_member_id from the client.

Security and permissions:
This endpoint requires authentication and is intended for the member actor. Implementations MUST rate-limit report creation to mitigate abuse and must validate target_type against supported domain values (e.g., 'article','comment','attachment').

Validation rules and business logic:
- Required inputs: target_type (string), target_id (UUID), reason_category (enum-like string such as 'Spam','Harassment','Misinformation','Illegal','Other').
- explanation is optional but must be length-limited (recommend max 1000 characters) and sanitized.
- If the uniqueness constraint (reporter_member_id + target_type + target_id) would be violated, return 409 Conflict with a clear message.
- The server sets status to 'pending' (or appropriate workflow default) and created_at timestamp.

Errors and expected behavior:
- 201 Created on success with the persisted report object including id and timestamps.
- 400 Bad Request for malformed target_id, unsupported target_type, missing reason_category, or explanation too long.
- 401 Unauthorized when no authenticated member is present.
- 409 Conflict when an identical report already exists from the same member.
- 500 Internal Server Error for unexpected failures; provide a correlation id for diagnostics.

requestBody.description: Report creation payload submitted by an authenticated member. The server will derive reporter_member_id from the authenticated principal and must ignore any client-supplied reporter_member_id if present.

responseBody.description: Created report record persisted to discussion_board_reports (includes id, target_type, target_id, reason_category, explanation, status and timestamps)

operations.name: create

prerequisites.description: When reporting an article as the target_type, the reported article must exist. POST /discussionBoard/member/articles creates the article resource referenced by target_id for reports that target articles.

When reporting a comment as the target_type, the comment must exist. POST /discussionBoard/member/articles/{articleId}/comments creates a comment linked to an article; the article must exist and the created comment provides the comment id usable as the report's target_id.

When reporting an attachment as the target_type, the attachment must exist. POST /discussionBoard/member/articles/{articleId}/attachments persists discussion_board_attachments metadata (provides the attachment id) which can be referenced by a report's target_id.

operations.specification: This operation retrieves a paginated, filterable list of moderation reports from the discussion_board_reports table in the Prisma schema. It is designed for moderator workflows to query and triage reports. The implementation is backed by the discussion_board_reports table which stores reporter_member_id, reporter_session_id, target_type, target_id, reason_category, explanation, status, created_at, processed_at and closed_at. The operation supports advanced search criteria (status, reason_category, reporterMemberId, targetType, targetId), date-range filters (created_at, processed_at), full-text search over explanation, sorting and pagination. Responses return a paginated summary view suitable for moderator queues and dashboards. Business rules: only moderator actors should access this endpoint; results must exclude closed reports by default and respect server-side pagination and max page size to limit expensive queries.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve paginated moderation reports from discussion_board_reports
operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of moderation reports for moderator triage and queue management. This operation queries the discussion_board_reports table and returns results in a paginated summary form optimized for moderator dashboards.

Security and permissions:
Access to this operation is restricted to moderator actors. Only authenticated moderators with appropriate privileges may call this endpoint. All reads should be recorded in moderation audit logs for accountability. The default response excludes closed reports unless the request explicitly requests closed=true.

Behavior and constraints:
- Accepts structured search request (IDiscussionBoardReport.IRequest) including pagination (page, limit), filters (status, reason_category, reporterMemberId, targetType, targetId), date ranges, text search over explanation, and sorting options.
- Server enforces max page size (recommended 100) to avoid expensive queries.
- By default returns non-closed reports (closed_at IS NULL) unless closed filter is set.
- Summaries include id, reporter_member_id, target_type, target_id, reason_category, status, created_at, processed_at, brief excerpt of explanation, and aggregated signals (e.g., uniqueReporterCount). Do NOT include reporter_session_id in the default summary to avoid exposing session-level detail; session id may be available in the detail endpoint under additional authorization checks.

Errors:
- 400 for invalid params; 404 for invalid referenced targets when used with strict mode; 503 for transient DB errors with correlation id.

requestBody.description: Search request parameters for moderator reports including pagination, filters (status, reason_category, reporterMemberId, targetType, targetId), date ranges, text search over explanation, and sorting options.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of report summaries from discussion_board_reports matching the search criteria. Each item contains summary fields useful for moderator queues (id, reporter_member_id, target_type, target_id, reason_category, status, created_at, processed_at, brief excerpt of explanation, uniqueReporterCount). Default summaries do NOT include reporter_session_id.

operations.name: index

operations.specification: This operation retrieves a single moderation report by primary key from discussion_board_reports. It returns the full report fields persisted at creation and processing time and optionally includes a capped set of related moderation actions and appeals for investigation. The operation is intended for moderator triage and audit review and must be guarded by RBAC and audit logging.
operations.summary: Retrieve a single moderation report by ID from discussion_board_reports
operations.description:
Return the detailed record of a moderation report stored in discussion_board_reports for use by moderators during triage. The response contains canonical fields: id, reporter_member_id, reporter_session_id (sensitive: include only id, not session payload), target_type (article|comment|attachment), target_id (UUID), reason_category (Spam|Harassment|Misinformation|Illegal|Other), explanation, status, created_at, processed_at and closed_at.

Security and permissions:
Only moderators may call this endpoint. Reads of report details and reporter identity MUST be recorded in moderation audit logs. If session-level details are required for investigation, include only reporter_session_id (id) and access must be additionally logged and restricted.

Relationships and embedding:
This endpoint may embed a capped list of related moderation actions and appeals (e.g., last 5) or provide links to full lists. Prefer links or paginated sub-resources for large related collections.

Validation:
- Path parameter reportId is a UUID and corresponds to discussion_board_reports.id. Return 400 for invalid UUID, 404 if not found.

Error handling:
- 400 invalid input; 403 unauthorized; 404 not found; 503 transient DB errors with correlation id.

parameters.name: reportId
parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the target report from discussion_board_reports.id

responseBody.description: Detailed moderation report record including persisted fields from discussion_board_reports and links or capped embedded references to related moderation actions and appeals.

operations.name: at

prerequisites.description: A report resource must exist before it can be retrieved by ID. Create the report using POST /discussionBoard/member/reports so the GET /discussionBoard/moderator/reports/{reportId} can return the persisted report.

operations.specification: Update a discussion board report record identified by reportId. This operation targets the discussion_board_reports table in the Prisma schema and allows moderators to update processing-related fields on an existing report. Implementation must update the report's status and relevant timestamp fields (processed_at and closed_at) as defined by the discussion_board_reports model. The operation preserves reporter identity and original report content while enabling moderators to record processing state transitions. The API must validate that the reportId exists and that the caller is authorized as a moderator. When updating status values, the implementation must validate against the canonical status vocabulary (for example 'pending','triaged','resolved') and ensure processed_at/closed_at are ISO 8601 timestamps. The operation must not expose session-level sensitive data (for example reporter session IP) in responses unless the caller has explicit audit privileges.
operations.summary: Update a report's processing status and timestamps (moderator only)
operations.description:
Purpose and overview:
This operation updates an existing report record in the discussion_board_reports table. Reports capture member-submitted complaints about articles, comments, or attachments (fields include reporter_member_id, reporter_session_id, target_type, target_id, reason_category, explanation, status, created_at, processed_at, closed_at). Moderators use this endpoint to record triage outcomes, change the report's processing status, and set processed/closed timestamps.

Security and permissions:
Only moderator actors are allowed to call this endpoint. The operation must verify the caller has moderator privileges and return 403 Forbidden for non-moderators. All changes must be recorded in the moderation audit subsystem (discussion_board_moderation_audit). Reporter session identifiers and IP addresses are considered sensitive and are redacted by default in responses; full session details are available only to authorized audit roles via separate audit APIs.

Relationship to database entity:
This operation maps directly to the discussion_board_reports model from the Prisma schema. The request updates the report's status, processed_at and closed_at columns. The operation MUST NOT assume additional fields exist on the report model (for example processed_by) and must not create or modify moderation action rows (those are created via discussion_board_moderation_actions).

Validation rules and business logic:
- Validate reportId is a UUID and that a report with the given id exists.
- Request status values must be validated against the canonical set enforced by the application (e.g., 'pending','triaged','resolved').
- processed_at and closed_at must be valid ISO 8601 timestamps if provided.
- Setting closed_at earlier than created_at MUST result in 400 Bad Request.
- Changing status to a resolved/closed state should set closed_at if not explicitly provided.

Expected behavior and error handling:
- 200 OK with the updated report when update succeeds.
- 400 Bad Request for validation errors (malformed timestamps, invalid status values, closed_at earlier than created_at).
- 401 Unauthorized when caller is not authenticated.
- 403 Forbidden when caller is authenticated but not a moderator.
- 404 Not Found when the reportId does not exist.

operations.specification: Retrieve a paginated list of reports associated with a single article (discussion_board_reports rows filtered by target_type='article' and target_id = articleId). Implemented as PATCH to support complex search criteria (status, reason_category, reporter_member_id, created/processed ranges, full-text search over explanation), sorting and pagination. Requires moderator privileges and returns report summaries suitable for a moderation queue. Sensitive session-level fields are redacted by default in summaries.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve paginated reports for a specific article (moderator only)
operations.description:
Purpose and overview:
This operation provides a flexible search and pagination interface to retrieve reports that target a specific article. The underlying Prisma entity is discussion_board_reports. This endpoint filters reports where target_type = 'article' and target_id = the given articleId and supports additional request-scoped filters passed in the request body.

Security considerations and user permissions:
Only moderator actors should access this endpoint because returned data may contain reporter identities and free-text explanations. The implementation must enforce moderator authorization and log access for audit purposes. Reporter session IPs and other session-level sensitive fields are redacted by default; inclusion requires elevated audit privileges.

Relationship to underlying database entities:
The response is derived from the discussion_board_reports table and may aggregate counts for automated thresholds. The operation does not modify the reports table. Returned summaries should include: id, reporter_member_id, reason_category, status, created_at, processed_at and explanationExcerpt. Full explanation text may be returned only with appropriate moderator-level access.

Validation rules and business logic:
- articleId must be a UUID corresponding to an existing discussion_board_articles.id.
- Request body may include filters: status (enum), reasonCategory, reporterMemberId (UUID), createdFrom/createdTo (ISO 8601), processedFrom/processedTo (ISO 8601), search (string), sort, page and limit.
- Pagination defaults: page=1, limit=20, max limit=100. Results include pagination metadata (total, page, limit).
- Implement query timeouts for heavy text searches and respect moderation endpoint rate limits.

Expected behavior and error handling:
- 200 OK with a paginated summary of matching reports.
- 400 Bad Request for invalid filter values or paging parameters.
- 401 Unauthorized if not authenticated.
- 403 Forbidden if authenticated but not a moderator.
- 404 Not Found if the articleId does not reference an existing article.

requestBody.description: Search and pagination parameters for retrieving reports targeting the specified article. Fields may include status, reasonCategory, reporterMemberId, createdFrom, createdTo, processedFrom, processedTo, search (free-text), page and limit.

responseBody.description: Paginated list (summary) of reports matching provided filters for the given article.

operations.name: index

POST /discussionBoard/member/articles creates a discussion_board_articles record; creating this article ensures the articleId path parameter refers to an existing article. If this prerequisite is not satisfied, the search will return 404 Not Found for the specified articleId.

operations.specification: Create a report record for a comment by inserting into the discussion_board_reports table in the Prisma schema. This operation maps directly to the discussion_board_reports model and captures reporter identity (reporter_member_id), optional reporter_session_id, the polymorphic target (target_type='comment' and target_id = commentId), reason_category, optional explanation, and created_at. It must respect the model-level unique constraint @@unique([reporter_member_id, target_type, target_id]) to prevent duplicate reports from the same member on the same comment. Downstream moderation workers will aggregate reports and apply automatic escalation policies (e.g., auto-hide when threshold reached).
operations.description:
Purpose and overview:

This operation allows an authenticated member to submit a report against a specific comment. The endpoint persists a new discussion_board_reports record with reporter_member_id derived from the authenticated user, optional reporter_session_id to help with fraud detection and audit correlation, a polymorphic target_type set to 'comment' and target_id equal to the path parameter commentId, and the chosen reason_category and explanation text. The created record is used by moderator queues and background aggregators to evaluate escalation thresholds.

Security and user permissions:

Only authenticated members may call this endpoint. The server implementation must extract and validate the caller's member identity and must prevent unauthenticated or moderator-only flows from using this member-scoped endpoint incorrectly. Rate limiting and anti-abuse heuristics should be applied per product policy.

Relationship to database entities and constraints:

This operation inserts into the Prisma model discussion_board_reports. Important referenced fields: reporter_member_id, reporter_session_id, target_type, target_id, reason_category, explanation, status (initially 'pending'), created_at. The database enforces @@unique([reporter_member_id, target_type, target_id]) which prevents duplicate reports by the same reporter for the same comment; the API should translate such constraint violations to HTTP 409 Conflict with a helpful message.

Validation and business rules:

- The commentId path parameter must refer to an existing discussion_board_comments.id; return 404 if not found.
- request body must include reason_category (one of 'Spam','Harassment','Misinformation','Illegal','Other') and may include explanation up to 1000 characters.
- The service sets created_at and status; clients MUST NOT supply those fields in the request.
- Duplicate reports by the same member for the same comment should result in 409 Conflict. The API may return the existing report id in that response to help clients.

Related operations:

- Moderator dashboards and GET /moderation/reports will consume this created record. Automated workers performing aggregation and auto-hide decisions act separately from this endpoint.

Errors and expected responses:

- 201 Created with the created IDiscussionBoardReport on success
- 400 Bad Request for validation failures
- 401 Unauthorized for unauthenticated callers
- 404 Not Found if the target comment does not exist
- 409 Conflict for duplicate report attempts

Implementation note:

Ensure the request processing derives reporter_member_id from the authenticated principal and validates reporter_session_id when provided. The endpoint should not allow clients to override system-managed fields.

responseBody.description: Created report record for the comment

operations.name: create

prerequisites.description: An article must exist before a comment can be created. Ensure an article is created so the comment (discussion_board_comments) can be attached to it; this supports subsequent creation of the comment referenced by commentId.

The comment referenced by commentId must exist before a report can be filed against it. Create the comment (discussion_board_comments) using the articleId parent so the report can reference a valid comment id.

operations.specification: Create a moderation action record in the discussion_board_moderation_actions table. This operation maps to the Prisma model discussion_board_moderation_actions and records the acting moderator id, optional originating report id, action_type (one of 'hide','remove','warn','suspend','ban'), optional action_reason, optional action_duration_days for time-limited sanctions, polymorphic target_type and target_id, and timestamps. The persisted moderation action is the canonical artifact for enforcement and auditing; enforcement workers must subscribe to events or check this table to apply side-effects (hide content, schedule suspensions, notify users).
operations.description:
Purpose and overview:

This endpoint enables a moderator to record and apply a moderation action. It persists a discussion_board_moderation_actions entry capturing moderator_id, optional discussion_board_report_id, action_type, action_reason, action_duration_days for temporary sanctions, and polymorphic target references (target_type + target_id). The moderation action record is auditable and is used as the source of truth for enforcement workers that apply content state changes or member sanctions.

Security and permissions:

Access to this endpoint is strictly limited to authenticated moderators. The service must validate moderator privileges prior to persisting the action. All moderation actions must also produce corresponding audit records in discussion_board_moderation_audit and emit events for enforcement subsystems.

Validation and business rules:

- moderator_id must be derived from the authenticated moderator principal; clients must not impersonate moderators.
- action_type must be one of the allowed values. Implementations must validate and reject unsupported action types.
- If discussion_board_report_id is supplied it must reference an existing report; otherwise return 400/404 as appropriate.
- When action_duration_days is supplied, compute effective_until as created_at + action_duration_days and schedule revocation accordingly.
- The endpoint returns 201 Created with the created moderation action; consumers (appeals, audit) will reference moderation_action.id.

Errors and expected responses:

- 201 Created with the created IDiscussionBoardModerationAction on success
- 400 Bad Request for validation failures
- 401/403 for authentication/authorization failures
- 404 Not Found for missing referenced resources

Implementation note:

Persist the moderation action and ensure an audit entry is created atomically or via a reliable outbox pattern.
operations.summary: Record a moderator action and trigger enforcement (discussion_board_moderation_actions)

requestBody.description: Moderation action creation payload

responseBody.description: Created moderation action record

operations.name: create

prerequisites.description: When discussion_board_report_id is supplied to the moderation action, the originating report must exist. Create the report (discussion_board_reports) so the moderation action can reference it as context for enforcement.

If the moderation action's target_type is 'article', the target article must exist. Create an article (discussion_board_articles) so the moderation action can reference a valid article id as target_id.

If the moderation action's target_type is 'comment', ensure the target comment exists by creating it (discussion_board_comments). This creates the comment under its parent article so the moderator can act on the comment target_id.

If the moderation action's target_type is 'attachment', ensure the attachment metadata exists (discussion_board_attachments) by creating attachments for an article so the moderation action can reference the attachment target_id.

operations.specification:
This operation implements a secure, pageable search and retrieval API for moderation actions stored in the Prisma table `discussion_board_moderation_actions`. It is a read-only, query-oriented endpoint that allows moderators to filter, sort and paginate moderation action records. The underlying data model is the `discussion_board_moderation_actions` table which contains columns such as `id`, `moderator_id`, `discussion_board_report_id`, `action_type`, `action_reason`, `action_duration_days`, `target_type`, `target_id`, `created_at`, `effective_from`, and `effective_until`. The operation may also join related entities for richer results (for example, resolving `moderator_id` to the `discussion_board_moderator` record or including the originating report referenced by `discussion_board_report_id`).

The operation supports complex search semantics (filter by moderator, action_type, target_type, date ranges on `created_at` or `effective_from`, and text search on `action_reason`), pagination (page, limit), and sorting (created_at, effective_from). Implementations should map the request DTO `IDiscussionBoardDiscussionBoardModerationAction.IRequest` to Prisma queries against `discussion_board_moderation_actions` and may include performant indexes such as the existing `@@index([moderator_id, created_at])` and `@@index([target_type, target_id])`. This operation should never expose internal-only fields from the moderation audit payloads unless the requesting moderator has sufficient privileges.

This operation is intended for moderator actors; results may be scoped or redacted depending on moderator privileges and organizational policies. Use database pagination and avoid returning raw, unbounded result sets. The operation returns a paginated summary container `IPageIDiscussionBoardDiscussionBoardModerationAction.ISummary` optimized for list displays.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve a filtered, paginated list of moderation actions (discussion_board_moderation_actions)
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated collection of moderation actions from the `discussion_board_moderation_actions` table.

This operation is designed for moderators to find moderation actions by multiple criteria: moderator id (`moderator_id`), originating report (`discussion_board_report_id`), action type (`action_type`, e.g., 'hide','remove','warn','suspend','ban'), target_type/target_id (polymorphic target), date ranges over `created_at` or `effective_from`, and free-text search over `action_reason`. The request DTO `IDiscussionBoardDiscussionBoardModerationAction.IRequest` should express pagination (page, limit), sort instructions, and filter predicates. The implementation should leverage existing indexes (e.g., `@@index([moderator_id, created_at])`, `@@index([target_type, target_id])`) to ensure efficient queries.

Security and permissions: Only authenticated moderators may call this endpoint (authorization actor: `moderator`). The response must be scoped to the caller's permissions. Fields that reveal sensitive investigation details should be redacted unless the moderator's role permits viewing full audit payloads. Access to some audit payloads may additionally require cross-checking the `discussion_board_moderation_audit` table and the moderator's audit access rights.

Relationship to database entities and validation: This operation maps directly to the `discussion_board_moderation_actions` Prisma model; valid filter fields must correspond to actual columns described in the Prisma schema (for example, `action_type`, `moderator_id`, `discussion_board_report_id`, `target_type`, `target_id`, `created_at`, `effective_from`, `effective_until`). The request DTO must NOT attempt to filter on non-existent columns. The response summaries should include safe subsets of the moderation action fields and small related objects (moderator summary, linked report summary) when authorized.

Related operations: Use `GET /moderation/actions/{actionId}` to retrieve a single moderation action with full details, including linked audit entries and the original report if present. Error handling: validate pagination parameters, return 400 for invalid filters, and return an empty page when no records match. Typical errors include 400 (bad request), 401 (unauthorized), and 403 (forbidden if moderator lacks privileges).

requestBody.description: Search, filter and pagination parameters for moderation actions. Use fields such as moderatorId, reportId, actionType, targetType, createdFrom, createdTo, page, limit, sort.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of moderation action summaries matching the search criteria.

operations.name: index

prerequisites.description: A persisted report must exist when the moderator search filters by reportId. Create the report via POST /discussionBoard/member/reports so the search can reference a valid discussion_board_reports.id. If this prerequisite fails, queries filtering by reportId will not find the expected report and may return empty results.

When moderation filters use a targetId that references an article, that article must exist. Create the article via POST /discussionBoard/member/articles to provide a valid discussion_board_articles.id as the targetId. If the article does not exist, filtering by that targetId will yield no matches or be considered invalid.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves a single moderation action by its primary key `id` from the Prisma table `discussion_board_moderation_actions`. The moderation action model includes the following representative columns: `id`, `moderator_id` (actor who performed the action), `discussion_board_report_id` (optional originating report), `action_type` (e.g., 'hide','remove','warn','suspend','ban'), `action_reason`, `action_duration_days`, `target_type`, `target_id`, `created_at`, `effective_from`, and `effective_until`.

The endpoint returns the full moderation action DTO `IDiscussionBoardDiscussionBoardModerationAction` and may, when authorized, include embedded summaries of related records such as the acting moderator (`discussion_board_moderator`) and the originating report (`discussion_board_reports`). Implementations should ensure that any inclusion of audit payloads or moderation audit entries is gated by the requesting moderator's permissions and that sensitive information is redacted when necessary.

This operation is intended strictly for moderator actors and should validate that the caller has sufficient privileges to view the requested record. If the requested action references a `discussion_board_report_id`, the implementation may also fetch related report metadata from `discussion_board_reports` and include it in the response according to access rules. Error handling: return 404 when the `actionId` does not exist, 401 for unauthenticated requests, and 403 when the moderator is not permitted to view the record.
operations.summary: Retrieve a single moderation action by id (discussion_board_moderation_actions)
operations.description:
Return detailed information for a single moderation action.

Purpose & overview: This operation provides moderators with the complete details of a moderation action recorded in `discussion_board_moderation_actions`. The response includes core fields such as `action_type`, `action_reason`, `action_duration_days`, `target_type`, `target_id`, timestamps (`created_at`, `effective_from`, `effective_until`) and references (`moderator_id`, `discussion_board_report_id`). When permitted, the response may also include a minimal moderator profile (id, username, display_name) and a brief linked report summary.

Security considerations and permissions: Access to this endpoint is restricted to moderator actors (`moderator`). Implementations must verify that the requesting moderator has the right to view the specific action and related context. If access is restricted, return 403. All calls must be authenticated and authorized; sensitive audit payloads referenced by this action should only be returned when the requesting moderator's privileges allow it.

Relationship to underlying database entities: This operation queries the Prisma `discussion_board_moderation_actions` model. If the moderation action references `discussion_board_report_id`, the service may join to the `discussion_board_reports` table to surface summary information (report reason_category, created_at) for context. For forensic reconstruction, callers should use the separate moderation audit endpoints which read `discussion_board_moderation_audit` records.

Validation rules and error handling: The path parameter `actionId` must be a UUID that corresponds to an existing moderation action. If not found, return 404. If the caller lacks permission, return 403. If the `actionId` format is invalid, return 400. Related operations: `PATCH /moderation/actions` for list/search and `GET /moderation/actions/{actionId}/audit` (not implemented here) for the audit trail details.

parameters.name: actionId
parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the target moderation action

responseBody.description: Detailed moderation action record including core fields and optional linked summaries (moderator, originating report) when authorized.

operations.name: at

operations.specification: Creates a new appeal in the discussion_board_appeals table. This maps directly to the Prisma model discussion_board_appeals and persists the following fields: appellant_member_id (server-populated from authenticated member), moderation_action_id (nullable FK to discussion_board_moderation_actions), report_id (nullable FK to discussion_board_reports), explanation (string, persisted), status (server-set to 'pending'), created_at (server timestamp). The operation MUST validate that at least one of moderation_action_id or report_id is provided and that any provided referenced ID exists. The implementation MUST NOT accept appellant_member_id from client payload and MUST derive the appellant identity from the authenticated token. On success the operation returns the persisted appeal record (IDiscussionBoardAppeal). On unique-constraint violation (duplicate appeal for same appellant+moderation_action_id or appellant+report_id) the implementation should return 409 Conflict. The operation also enqueues a moderator review task and creates an internal moderation audit entry (stored via discussion_board_moderation_audit) — these side effects are system-generated and must be implemented in service logic (not exposed as separate public APIs).
operations.summary: Create a new appeal (persist to discussion_board_appeals)
operations.description:
Create a new appeal submitted by a member contesting a moderation action or a report.

Purpose and overview: This endpoint creates an appeal record in the discussion_board_appeals table. Appeals are an append-only business artifact used to request secondary review of moderator actions or reports. The appeal record stores the appellant_member_id (populated from the authenticated caller), optional moderation_action_id, optional report_id, the appellant-provided explanation, and a processing status 'pending'. The created record is used to queue secondary review tasks for moderators and to pause purge timers for the underlying content while the appeal is pending.

Security and permissions: Only authenticated members may submit appeals. The API MUST authenticate the caller (requesting member) and use the caller's identity as appellant_member_id. The endpoint MUST NOT accept or honor an appellant_member_id in the request payload to prevent identity injection. Moderation/administrative actors should not call this endpoint on behalf of other members; administrative workflows exist separately.

Relationship to the Prisma table: This operation directly maps to the Prisma model discussion_board_appeals. The implementation must persist only the model fields: appellant_member_id, moderation_action_id, report_id, explanation, status, created_at, resolved_at, resolution_reason. Do NOT invent fields not present in the model. The operation should validate referenced IDs exist (when provided) and return 400 when they do not.

Validation rules and business logic:
- explanation is required (<= 2000 chars as per business rules).
- At least one of moderation_action_id or report_id MUST be present.
- status is set to 'pending' server-side and clients cannot set resolved statuses on create.
- created_at is server-populated; clients must not supply created_at or resolved_at values.

Related operations: Moderators will query appeals via PATCH /discussionBoard/moderator/appeals and will resolve appeals with moderation action endpoints. When an appeal is created the system should also emit a moderation_audit entry and push the item onto the moderator queue for handling.

Errors and handling: 400 for validation errors (missing explanation or missing referenced id), 401/403 for auth failures, 404 if referenced moderation_action_id/report_id do not exist, 409 for unique-constraint duplicate appeals, 500 for server errors.

requestBody.description: Appeal creation payload. Clients MUST provide: explanation (string) and at least one of moderation_action_id (uuid) or report_id (uuid). Do NOT include appellant_member_id, created_at, resolved_at or status in the payload; those are managed by the server.

responseBody.description: Created appeal record representing the persisted discussion_board_appeals row. Contains persisted id, moderation_action_id/report_id references, explanation, status='pending', created_at timestamp and nullable resolved_at/resolution_reason.

operations.name: create

Create the report first (POST /discussionBoard/member/reports) so the appeal can reference a valid discussion_board_reports.id. If this prerequisite fails, any appeal attempted with report_id will be invalid (404) or rejected.

If the appeal references a moderation_action_id the referenced moderation action must already exist. Create the moderation action first (POST /discussionBoard/moderator/moderation/actions) to obtain a valid discussion_board_moderation_actions.id for the appeal.
