operations.specification: Retrieves a paginated, filterable list of appeals from the discussion_board_appeals table for moderator triage. Supports filters: status list, appellant_member_id, moderation_action_id, report_id, created_at date ranges and free-text search on explanation. Results return summary DTOs and pagination metadata. Implementation must enforce role-based access (moderator), record an audit access entry for the moderator query, and enforce maximum page size and efficient pagination to protect the system.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve paginated appeals for moderator triage (discussion_board_appeals)
operations.description:
Search and list appeals for moderator triage and management.

Purpose and overview: This read-only endpoint allows moderators to retrieve a paginated collection of appeals from the discussion_board_appeals model. The operation supports filtering by status (pending, accepted, rejected, etc.), filtering by appellant_member_id, related moderation_action_id or report_id, as well as creation time ranges and optional full-text search on the explanation field. Results are returned in a paginated summary format optimized for moderator queues.

Security and permissions: Access to this endpoint is restricted to moderators and administrative actors. The implementation MUST enforce authentication and role checks (moderator role). For auditability, every listing request MUST create an audit access record (discussion_board_audit_log_accesses) capturing the requesting moderator id and the query parameters used.

Relationship to Prisma table: This operation reads from discussion_board_appeals and may join to related models (discussion_board_moderation_actions, discussion_board_reports, discussion_board_member) to populate safe summary fields such as appellant display_name and referenced action/report short info. Do not return moderator-only internal notes.

Filtering, pagination and sorting:
- Request body (IDiscussionBoardAppeal.IRequest) supports page/limit (with enforced maxPageSize server-side), status list, appellant_member_id, moderation_action_id, report_id, created_at_from, created_at_to, sort parameters and optional cursor for seek pagination.
- Response uses a paginated container IPageIDiscussionBoardAppeal.ISummary containing pagination metadata and an array of appeal summary objects.

Validation and behavior:
- Invalid filter values produce 400 responses with descriptive validation messages.
- Default sort = -created_at (most recent first).
- Enforce a conservative maximum page size (recommendation: 200) to prevent large scans. Use seek pagination (cursor) for high-volume workloads.

Related operations: Use POST /discussionBoard/member/appeals for creation and moderation action endpoints for resolving appeals. When appeals are resolved the moderator should call the appropriate moderation action endpoints which will update the appeal's status and resolved_at timestamp.

requestBody.description: Search criteria, filters and pagination parameters for retrieving appeals. Use pagination parameters and limit page size to server-allowed maximum.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of appeal summaries (IPageIDiscussionBoardAppeal.ISummary), includes pagination metadata and an array of safe summary objects for moderator triage.

operations.name: index

prerequisites.description: When moderator filters include report_id, the referenced report must exist. Ensure a report is created via POST /discussionBoard/member/reports so the report_id filter can match an existing discussion_board_reports.id; otherwise the listing filter would yield 404/no-results or be invalid.

When moderator filters include moderation_action_id, the referenced moderation action must exist. Create the moderation action via POST /discussionBoard/moderator/moderation/actions so the moderation_action_id filter can match an existing discussion_board_moderation_actions.id. Order: create report (if applicable) before creating moderation action when the action depends on a report.

operations.specification: Retrieve a single discussion_board_appeals row by primary key (id). This operation queries the discussion_board_appeals Prisma model and returns the appeal object used in the moderation/appeals workflow. Implementation must validate appealId as UUID, enforce ownership authorization (member can access own appeals; moderators use moderator endpoints), and return only fields present in the Prisma model.
operations.summary: Retrieve a DiscussionBoard appeal by ID (discussion_board_appeals)
operations.description:
Purpose and overview:

Retrieve a single appeal record stored in the discussion_board_appeals table. The appeal contains appellant_member_id, optional links to moderation_action and/or report, the appellant's explanation, processing status and resolution metadata. Clients use this endpoint to display appeal details and timelines to the appellant and to support member-facing appeal status pages.

Security and permissions:

This endpoint requires authentication as a member. The implementation MUST enforce that a member may retrieve only their own appeals (owner check: appeal.appellant_member_id === auth.memberId). Moderators should use dedicated moderator endpoints to retrieve any appeal. Do not expose internal audit trails in this member-facing response.

Validation rules and error handling:

- Validate that the path parameter appealId is a well-formed UUID; return 400 for invalid format.
- If the appeal is not found, return 404 with an explanatory message.
- Enforce authorization: return 403 when an unauthorized member attempts to access another member's appeal.

Related operations:

- PUT /discussionBoard/moderator/appeals/{appealId} — moderator updates to appeal status and resolution metadata.

parameters.name: appealId

operations.specification: Update mutable fields of an existing discussion_board_appeals row. Intended for moderators to record appeal resolutions (status, resolution_reason, resolved_at) and to optionally associate a moderation_action_id. Implementation must validate status transitions, ensure referenced moderation_action exists when provided, validate resolved_at chronology, and append an audit entry in discussion_board_moderation_audit via service logic.
operations.summary: Update a DiscussionBoard appeal (discussion_board_appeals) — moderator action
operations.description:
Purpose and overview:

Allows privileged moderators to update an appeal's mutable properties in the discussion_board_appeals table. Typical updates include status transitions (e.g., 'pending' → 'accepted'|'rejected'), resolution_reason text, resolved_at timestamp, and optional moderation_action_id linking the resolution to a concrete moderation action. The endpoint returns the updated appeal record.

Security and permissions:

Only moderator actors are authorized to call this endpoint. Implementations MUST authenticate the caller as a moderator and MUST record the acting moderator id in moderation audit trails (discussion_board_moderation_audit). Unauthorized callers must receive a 403 Forbidden response.

Validation rules, referential integrity and business logic:

- Validate appealId is a UUID; return 400 if invalid.
- Reject requests that attempt disallowed status transitions (for example moving from 'accepted' back to 'pending' without an explicative reason), returning 400 with details.
- If moderation_action_id is provided, ensure the referenced moderation action exists (discussion_board_moderation_actions); if the referenced action conflicts with current appeal state, return 409 Conflict.
- When setting resolved_at, validate it is an ISO 8601 datetime not earlier than created_at.

Side effects and audit:

After a successful update, the implementation SHOULD append an audit entry to discussion_board_moderation_audit capturing moderator id, action details and before/after appeal state. If appeal resolution changes content visibility or retention timers, update related content workflows accordingly.

This prerequisite validates referential integrity for the moderation action (discussion_board_moderation_actions); if it fails, the update should return 400/404/409 as appropriate.

The appeal must exist before it can be updated. This prerequisite ensures the target discussion_board_appeals row is present; if missing the update should return 404 and no mutable fields are applied.

operations.specification: This operation implements a global, cross-entity search composed from multiple Prisma models: discussion_board_articles, discussion_board_comments, discussion_board_attachments, discussion_board_tags, and discussion_board_member. It provides a single entry point for free-text and filtered search across article titles and bodies, comment text, tag names, and author display names. The implementation will execute composed queries (full-text or trigram-based searches using the indexed title/content/comment fields and tag/name indexes) and return a paginated, type-safe result set. The operation does NOT modify any database rows; it is a read-only search endpoint that aggregates results from multiple Prisma models and presents a unified result shape (IDiscussionBoardSearchResult) for client consumption.
operations.summary: Search across articles, comments, attachments, tags and authors
operations.description:
Purpose and overview:

This operation provides a single, global search endpoint that satisfies user needs for "search everything" across the discussion board. It composes queries across the discussion_board_articles (title, content), discussion_board_comments (content), discussion_board_tags (name/slug via the junction table discussion_board_article_tags), discussion_board_attachments (original_filename), and discussion_board_member (username and display_name) models defined in the Prisma schema. The search leverages the existing GIN/trigram indexes on title, content, and indexed name fields to deliver performant full-text or similarity search.

Security and permissions:

The endpoint is public by default (authorizationActors = []). Public search results must respect content state rules from the Content schema: only articles with state = 'published' and comments/attachments that are not hidden or quarantined are returned. The service implementation must filter out soft-deleted records (deleted_at != null) and moderation-hidden content (is_hidden / state) according to the rules in the database models. The endpoint returns only fields appropriate for public consumption; sensitive fields (e.g., member.email, password_hash) are never exposed.

Data relationships and behavior:

Results combine multiple underlying tables into a unified result type IDiscussionBoardSearchResult. Each result object includes a discriminator "type" ("article" | "comment" | "attachment" | "tag") and a minimal payload referencing the originating entity (id, title/excerpt or filename, author summary when applicable, created_at). When the result refers to an article, it includes article summary fields derived from discussion_board_articles (title, excerpt from content, is_pinned, published_at). When the result refers to a comment, it includes the comment content excerpt and the parent article reference. Tag results include tag name and slug from discussion_board_tags. Attachment results include original_filename and is_image from discussion_board_attachments. Author references use discussion_board_member.username and display_name only.

Validation rules and request options:

The request body (IDiscussionBoardSearch.IRequest) supports:
- query (string): required for full-text matching; must be non-empty
- filters: optional object allowing entity-type filtering (articles, comments, attachments, tags), category filter by discussion_board_category_id, tag slugs, author username, date ranges (created_from/created_to) mapped to ISO8601 datetimes
- pagination: page, limit (limit capped at 100)
- sorting: relevance (default), newest (created_at/published_at descending), oldest
- highlight: optional boolean to request highlighted snippets for matched fields

Related API operations:

Clients typically call GET /articles/{id} to obtain full article details for selected article search results, or GET /articles/{id}?includeComments=true to fetch comments. Attachment downloads are performed via GET /attachments/{id}/download. This global search operation is read-only and intended to guide navigation to those resource-specific endpoints.

Expected behavior and error handling:

- Empty or whitespace-only query must return HTTP 400 with a clear validation message.
- Results must exclude soft-deleted records (deleted_at not null), moderation-hidden items (state != 'published' for articles, is_hidden = true for comments, quarantined = true for comment attachments), and quarantined attachments.
- Pagination metadata (total, page, limit) must be returned alongside result list. Partial results are possible when data sources respond at different latencies; the implementation should favor consistent snapshot semantics for the query.

Implementation note (SQL/Prisma guidance):

A sample implementation may perform parallel queries against each model using Prisma where clauses and indexed full-text/trigram operations, then merge results with relevance scoring. Example (conceptual):

SELECT id, 'article' as type, title, ts_rank_cd(article_search_vector, plainto_tsquery($1)) as rank
FROM discussion_board_articles
WHERE state = 'published' AND (title ILIKE '%'||$1||'%' OR content ILIKE '%'||$1||'%')
ORDER BY rank DESC, published_at DESC

This operation is read-only and maps to the IDiscussionBoardSearchResult response DTO.

requestBody.description: Search criteria, filters and pagination parameters for the global search across articles, comments, attachments and tags.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of unified search results matching the query. Each result contains a discriminator type and a minimal payload linking back to its original resource (article, comment, attachment, tag).

operations.name: search

prerequisites.description: A Category must exist before it can be referenced by categoryId in search filters. Create the category via POST /discussionBoard/moderator/categories so the search can accept a valid categoryId; if the category does not exist searches filtered by categoryId would be invalid or return no results.

operations.specification: This operation computes article activity statistics by aggregating data from the discussion_board_articles, discussion_board_comments, and discussion_board_attachments tables defined in the Prisma schema. It produces time-series metrics (e.g., daily counts of published articles, comments, and attachments) to support dashboards and trend analysis. The operation is read-only and derives metrics from published and non-deleted records only.
operations.summary: Retrieve time-series statistics of article activity (articles, comments, attachments)
operations.description:
Purpose and overview:

This read-only endpoint returns aggregated article activity statistics intended for dashboards and analytic views. It computes metrics such as published article count, comment count, attachment uploads, and derived KPIs (average comments per article, top tags) over a configurable time range. The operation references the discussion_board_articles, discussion_board_comments, discussion_board_attachments and discussion_board_article_tags (for tag aggregation) models in the Prisma schema.

Security and permissions:

The endpoint is public (authorizationActors = []) for read-only dashboards that display aggregated, non-sensitive metrics. Returned data contains only aggregated numbers and safe, non-identifying tag labels; no personal data such as member.email or password_hash is returned. The implementation must exclude soft-deleted articles and items (deleted_at not null) and exclude moderation-hidden items (state != 'published' and quarantined flags) from the aggregates.

Relationship to underlying database entities and business rules:

The statistics are derived as follows:
- article_count: COUNT of discussion_board_articles where state = 'published' and deleted_at IS NULL and published_at between requested range
- comment_count: COUNT of discussion_board_comments where deleted_at IS NULL and is_hidden = false and created_at within range and whose article parent is in published state (join to discussion_board_articles)
- attachment_count: COUNT of discussion_board_attachments where deleted_at IS NULL and created_at within range and whose article is published
- average_comments_per_article: comment_count / NULLIF(article_count,0)
- top_tags: aggregation joining discussion_board_article_tags -> discussion_board_tags to find most-used tag slugs/names in the period

Validation rules and request parameters:

This GET operation accepts optional query parameters for start_date and end_date (ISO 8601). If omitted, the implementation defaults to the last 30 days. The service should validate date formats and return HTTP 400 for invalid dates. The response DTO IDiscussionBoardArticleActivityStatistics contains the requested time-bucketed series (e.g., daily array) and overall summary metrics.

Expected behavior and error handling:

- If start_date is after end_date, return HTTP 400 with a descriptive message.
- If there is no data in the requested period, return an empty series and zeros for counts.
- The statistics must be computed from current committed data and reflect the same moderation filtering rules used elsewhere (exclude soft-deleted or hidden content).

Implementation note (SQL guidance):

A typical implementation uses a GROUP BY time_bucket (day/week/month) on the article.created_at or published_at field and joins comments/attachments to compute counts. Example conceptual SQL for daily aggregation:

SELECT date_trunc('day', published_at) AS day,
       COUNT(DISTINCT a.id) AS article_count,
       COUNT(DISTINCT c.id) AS comment_count,
       COUNT(DISTINCT att.id) AS attachment_count
FROM discussion_board_articles a
LEFT JOIN discussion_board_comments c ON c.discussion_board_article_id = a.id AND c.deleted_at IS NULL AND c.is_hidden = false AND c.created_at BETWEEN $start AND $end
LEFT JOIN discussion_board_attachments att ON att.discussion_board_article_id = a.id AND att.deleted_at IS NULL AND att.created_at BETWEEN $start AND $end
WHERE a.state = 'published' AND a.deleted_at IS NULL AND a.published_at BETWEEN $start AND $end
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1 DESC

This operation returns an IDiscussionBoardArticleActivityStatistics response.

responseBody.description: Time-series and summary metrics of article activity (articles, comments, attachments) for the requested date range.

operations.name: articleActivity

operations.specification: This operation computes monthly article publication statistics by aggregating data from the discussion_board_articles table in the Prisma schema. It performs a time-bucket aggregation on discussion_board_articles.published_at (group by month) and computes counts per state and simple derived metrics. Only fields that actually exist in the Prisma schema are referenced: discussion_board_articles.published_at, discussion_board_articles.state, discussion_board_articles.discussion_board_member_id, discussion_board_articles.deleted_at. The aggregation excludes rows where deleted_at IS NOT NULL to respect soft-delete retention. Implementers should use DATE_TRUNC('month', published_at) (or equivalent) and conditional aggregations for each state value (draft, published, pending_review, hidden). When computing average articles per author, count unique discussion_board_member_id per month as denominator. This endpoint is read-only and intended for dashboards. Consider caching and rate-limiting for heavy datasets.
operations.summary: Retrieve monthly aggregated article statistics (DiscussionBoard - computed from discussion_board_articles)
operations.description:
Purpose and overview: Compute monthly aggregates for articles by grouping discussion_board_articles by calendar month using the published_at timestamp. This operation returns one entry per month containing counts broken down by state (published, draft, pending_review, hidden), the total articles published that month, the number of distinct authors who published that month, and derived metrics such as average_published_per_author.

Security considerations and user permissions: This is a read-only aggregation. Results may be considered sensitive for some product contexts; restrict access to staff or admin dashboards if needed. The operation excludes soft-deleted articles (discussion_board_articles.deleted_at IS NOT NULL) to honor retention rules.

Relationship to DB entities: Maps to the discussion_board_articles Prisma model. Implementation MUST reference only existing columns: published_at, state, discussion_board_member_id, created_at, deleted_at. Do not assume additional audit columns exist beyond those defined in the schema.

Validation rules and business logic: Validate optional query filters (dateFrom, dateTo) as ISO 8601 dates. If published_at is null for drafts, those rows belong to draft counts and may be included depending on date filter semantics; implementers should document chosen semantics. Error handling: return 5xx for DB errors with correlation id; return empty array for no-data results.

Related operations: Use along with admin dashboards and the audit logs search endpoint for investigation. Consider a precomputed materialized view for production-scale datasets.

responseBody.description: Array of monthly statistics objects ordered by month descending. Each object contains: month (ISO 8601 string at month start), published_count, draft_count, pending_review_count, hidden_count, distinct_authors_published, average_published_per_author.

operations.name: articlesByMonth

operations.specification: Search and retrieve paginated audit log entries from the discussion_board_audit_logs table. This operation accepts advanced filters and full-text search over the metadata column, leveraging the GIN/trigram indexes defined in the Prisma schema. It is explicitly tied to the discussion_board_audit_logs model and must respect sensitivity: audit logs are append-only and intended for privileged access only. The implementation should validate date ranges, enforce maximum page sizes, and redact sensitive metadata for callers without elevated permission.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve paginated audit log entries (DiscussionBoard - discussion_board_audit_logs)
operations.description:
Purpose and overview: Provide a flexible search endpoint for audit records captured in discussion_board_audit_logs. Supported filters include event_type, actor_type, actor_id, resource_type, resource_id, dateFrom/dateTo, and a full-text 'fullText' search over metadata. Results are paginated and ordered by event_timestamp by default.

Security considerations and user permissions: Audit logs contain sensitive data; access MUST be restricted to authorized actors. Every access to audit logs must be recorded in discussion_board_audit_log_accesses per policy. Responses should redact sensitive metadata unless the caller has explicit permission.

Relationship to DB entities: Operates on discussion_board_audit_logs and should use indexes on event_timestamp, actor_type/actor_id and resource_type/resource_id. Use the metadata GIN/trgm index for efficient full-text search.

Validation and business logic: Enforce date range validation and a maximum limit (e.g., limit <= 100). Provide clear error messages for invalid filters. For very large exports, provide an asynchronous export mechanism rather than returning massive result sets synchronously.

requestBody.description: Search request for audit logs including optional filters, pagination and sorting. Fields: eventType, actorType, actorId, resourceType, resourceId, fullText, dateFrom, dateTo, page (int), limit (int).

responseBody.description: Paginated results containing audit log summaries and pagination metadata.

operations.name: index

prerequisites.description: If the audit log query filters by a resourceId that refers to an Article, an Article record must exist. POST /discussionBoard/member/articles creates the discussion_board_articles row (providing an article id) so the audit search can match audit entries that reference that article. This ensures the resourceId corresponds to a persisted article and yields meaningful audit results.

If the audit log query filters by a resourceId that refers to a Comment, a Comment record must exist. POST /discussionBoard/member/articles/{articleId}/comments creates a discussion_board_comments row (providing a comment id) tied to an article; creating the parent article (POST /discussionBoard/member/articles) before this is required so the comment can be created and later matched by audit entries.

If the audit log query filters by a resourceId that refers to an Attachment, an Attachment metadata row must exist. POST /discussionBoard/member/articles/{articleId}/attachments persists discussion_board_attachments metadata (providing an attachment id) linked to an article; creating the parent article (POST /discussionBoard/member/articles) first ensures the attachment can be created and referenced by audit log entries.

operations.specification: Retrieve a single audit log record from the Prisma table `discussion_board_audit_logs`. This operation reads the append-only audit entry identified by the provided auditLogId (UUID) and returns the stored audit record. It maps directly to the Prisma model `discussion_board_audit_logs`. Implementation notes: validate UUID format, enforce authorization (only privileged moderator/compliance actors may view full unredacted payload), record the read operation in `discussion_board_audit_log_accesses` (create an access entry) for auditing, and apply PII redaction policies to the metadata field for callers without explicit unredacted privileges.
operations.summary: Retrieve a single audit log record (discussion_board_audit_logs)
operations.description:
Purpose and overview:

Retrieve a single append-only audit record from the discussion_board_audit_logs table. The audit log stores system and user events for compliance and investigations; this endpoint returns the canonical forensic snapshot for the specified auditLogId, including event_type, event_timestamp, resource_type/resource_id, actor_type/actor_id, ip, user_agent, metadata, and created/updated timestamps as recorded in the database.

Security considerations and permissions:

Access to audit records is highly sensitive and MUST be restricted to authorized moderator/compliance actors. The service MUST perform authorization checks before returning any data. Implementations MUST record the read access by creating an entry in discussion_board_audit_log_accesses including accessor_type, accessor_id, accessor_role, access_purpose (if provided), ip, user_agent and accessed_at. The `metadata` field may contain PII and MUST be redacted for callers without explicit unredacted-audit privileges; the API response contract may therefore return a redacted `metadata` or an indication that redaction was applied.

Relationship to underlying database entities:

This operation maps directly to the Prisma model `discussion_board_audit_logs`. Returned fields correspond to model columns such as id, event_type, event_timestamp, resource_type, resource_id, actor_type, actor_id, ip, user_agent, metadata, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at. Implementations should not modify the audit row (append-only semantics).

Validation rules and business logic:

- Validate that the provided auditLogId is a well-formed UUID.
- Confirm the record exists; return 404 when missing.
- Enforce authorization: only privileged users may view the full payload; other moderator roles may receive a redacted view.
- The operation MUST create an audit-access record capturing the read (discussion_board_audit_log_accesses).
- The operation MUST not alter the audit row itself.

Related operations and error handling:

Related operation: PATCH /discussionBoard/moderator/auditLogs/{auditLogId}/accesses returns access history for the audit record. Common errors: 400 (invalid UUID), 401 (unauthenticated), 403 (forbidden), 404 (not found), 500 (internal error).

parameters.name: auditLogId
parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the target audit log entry in discussion_board_audit_logs (UUID)

responseBody.description: Detailed audit log record as stored in the discussion_board_audit_logs Prisma model (note: metadata may be redacted based on caller privileges)

operations.name: at

operations.specification: Retrieve a paginated list of audit-log-access entries from the Prisma table `discussion_board_audit_log_accesses` for a given audit log id. This operation supports search, filtering, sorting and pagination over access records that show who accessed a particular audit log entry. Implementation MUST validate auditLogId, enforce authorization, apply PII redaction rules for accessor_id/ip/user_agent/metadata based on caller privileges, and enforce pagination limits. The underlying model is `discussion_board_audit_log_accesses` and returned items map to that model's fields.
operations.summary: List access audit entries for a specific audit log (discussion_board_audit_log_accesses)
operations.description:
Purpose and overview:

Return a paginated, filterable list of audit-log-access events related to the specified audit log entry. Each access record represents a read/access event against an audit log (append-only access entries). This endpoint supports pagination, filtering by accessor_type, accessor_id, access_purpose, and date ranges, and sorting by accessed_at.

Security considerations and user permissions:

Access to audit-access records is restricted to privileged actors (moderators or other authorized roles). The response contains metadata about who accessed sensitive audit records; implementations MUST enforce strict authorization and MUST redact fields (accessor_id, ip, user_agent, metadata) for callers without explicit unredacted-audit privileges. Calls to this endpoint SHOULD be recorded in an operational audit and the act of retrieving these rows is itself auditable.

Relationship to underlying database entities:

This operation queries the Prisma model `discussion_board_audit_log_accesses` filtered by discussion_board_audit_log_id = {auditLogId}. Returned items map to model fields such as id, discussion_board_audit_log_id, accessed_at, accessor_type, accessor_id, accessor_role, access_purpose, ip, user_agent, metadata and created_at. The query should leverage indexes on (discussion_board_audit_log_id, accessed_at) for efficient retrieval.

Validation rules and business logic:

- Validate auditLogId is a UUID and that the referenced audit log exists and is accessible to the requesting actor.
- Support pagination parameters (page, limit) in the request body; server should enforce sensible defaults and maximum page sizes to prevent expensive queries.
- Ensure returned items respect redaction and privacy rules for PII in metadata and requester-specific visibility rules.

Related operations and error handling:

Related operation: GET /discussionBoard/moderator/auditLogs/{auditLogId} returns the audit record itself. Common errors: 400 (invalid request/filter), 401 (unauthenticated), 403 (forbidden), 404 (audit log not found), 500 (internal error).

parameters.name: auditLogId
parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the target audit log entry (scoped to access records) (UUID)

requestBody.description: Search, filtering and pagination parameters for audit-log-access entries (do NOT include auditLogId in the body; it is provided in the path). Include page/limit, optional filters: accessor_type, accessor_id, access_purpose, date range.

responseBody.description: Paginated results container with summaries of audit-log-access entries (note: sensitive fields may be redacted depending on caller privileges)

operations.name: index

operations.specification: Retrieves a single audit-log-access record from the Prisma table discussion_board_audit_log_accesses. This read-only operation returns the persisted audit-access snapshot (id, discussion_board_audit_log_id, accessed_at, accessor_type, accessor_id, accessor_role, access_purpose, ip, user_agent, metadata, created_at, deleted_at) and is intended for moderator/audit use. Associated Prisma model: discussion_board_audit_log_accesses.
operations.summary: Retrieve a single DiscussionBoard audit-log-access record
operations.description:
Retrieve a single audit-log-access record that documents when an actor accessed an audit log entry.

Security and permissions:
Access to audit-log-access records is highly sensitive and restricted to privileged moderator roles. Implementations MUST enforce RBAC and may apply field-level redaction (for example: redact `metadata` or `accessor_id` for non-full-audit-role callers). Access to unredacted payloads must itself be logged in the system audit trail.

Relationship to DB entity:
This operation reads from discussion_board_audit_log_accesses and returns the stored columns. If a record has `deleted_at` set, the service should follow policy (either return 404 or permit return only to highest-privilege actors). Validate the UUID format for the path parameter and return 400 for invalid UUIDs.

Errors:
- 200: Returns the audit access record when found and authorized.
- 400: Invalid UUID format.
- 401/403: Unauthorized or insufficient privileges.
- 404: Not found or suppressed by retention/legal hold.
- 500: Server error; include correlation id for troubleshooting.

parameters.name: auditLogAccessId
parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the target audit-log-access record in discussion_board_audit_log_accesses (global primary key).

responseBody.description: Detailed audit-log-access record returned from discussion_board_audit_log_accesses

operations.name: at

operations.specification: Performs a filtered, sorted, and paginated search over moderation audit entries stored in the Prisma model discussion_board_moderation_audit. Supports filters: event_type, actor_moderator_id, moderation_action_id, report_id, occurred_at range, and free-text (textSearch) against event_payload. Returns paginated summaries (IPageIDiscussionBoardModerationAudit.ISummary) suitable for moderator dashboards. Associated Prisma model: discussion_board_moderation_audit.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve paginated moderation audit entries
operations.description:
Provide a flexible search API for moderation audit entries. Intended for moderators and investigators to query historical moderation events. The request body supports filters (eventType, moderatorId, reportId, moderationActionId), time range (occurredFrom, occurredTo), free-text `textSearch` for payloads and pagination parameters (page, limit, sort). Implementations MUST validate UUIDs and datetimes, enforce pagination defaults and maximum limits (e.g., default limit 20, max limit 100) and protect full-text queries with rate limits or privilege checks.

Security and permissions:
Access MUST be restricted to moderator actors. `event_payload` may contain sensitive content; unless the caller has full audit privileges, the service SHOULD redact or truncate `event_payload` in results. Requests that include free-text searches on `event_payload` SHOULD be rate-limited or require elevated privileges.

Errors:
- 200: Returns paginated list of moderation audit summaries.
- 400: Invalid filter formats or pagination parameters.
- 401/403: Unauthorized.
- 500: Server error. Include correlation id.

requestBody.description: Search criteria, filtering, pagination and sorting parameters for moderation audit entries (eventType, moderatorId, reportId, moderationActionId, occurredFrom, occurredTo, textSearch, page, limit, sort).

responseBody.description: Paginated list of moderation audit summary records (summary excludes or redacts full event_payload unless caller has privilege).

operations.name: index

prerequisites.description: A report record must exist before it can be referenced by moderation audit entries. Create a report (discussion_board_reports) so that filtering moderation audits by reportId can return relevant audit records. If this prerequisite fails, searches filtering by the reportId will yield no results.

A moderation action must exist before it can be referenced by moderation audit entries. Create a moderation action (discussion_board_moderation_actions) so that filtering moderation audits by moderationActionId will match persisted audit records. This should be executed after creating any originating report that the moderation action references.

operations.specification: This operation retrieves a single moderation audit entry from the discussion_board_moderation_audit Prisma model. It returns immutable audit data used for forensic reconstruction: id, moderation_action_id, report_id, actor_moderator_id, event_type, event_payload, occurred_at. Implementations MUST enforce RBAC (only moderator or higher roles). Each successful read MUST be recorded in discussion_board_audit_log_accesses (accessor_type, accessor_id, access_purpose, accessed_at). The event_payload field may contain sensitive data; the service MUST either redact sensitive fields before returning to general moderator roles or restrict raw payload access to elevated roles. The operation performs a read-only lookup by primary key and returns 404 when not found.
operations.summary: Retrieve a single moderation audit entry (discussion_board_moderation_audit)
operations.description:
Retrieve a single moderation audit entry by its identifier from the append-only moderation audit table.

Purpose and overview: Returns the immutable audit entry captured in discussion_board_moderation_audit. This data is used for investigations and compliance. The canonical stored payload (event_payload) is returned according to the caller's privilege level: raw payload only for elevated admin roles; moderated summary or redacted payload for standard moderator roles.

Security considerations and user permissions: Access is restricted to authorized moderator or administrative actors. The service MUST log every access to this endpoint in discussion_board_audit_log_accesses with accessor id, accessor role, access_purpose (e.g., 'investigation'), ip, and timestamp. Implement server-side redaction or privilege checks to avoid leaking reporter contact information or other PII inside event_payload.

Relationship to underlying database entities: Maps directly to the Prisma model discussion_board_moderation_audit and returns the stored fields: moderation_action_id, report_id, actor_moderator_id, event_type, event_payload, occurred_at.

Validation rules and business logic: Path parameter moderationAuditId is required and must be a UUID. Return codes: 200 with the audit entry (subject to redaction rules), 401 unauthorized, 403 forbidden (insufficient role), 404 not found, 500 internal error.

parameters.name: moderationAuditId
parameters.description: UUID identifier of the target moderation audit entry

responseBody.description: Moderation audit entry corresponding to discussion_board_moderation_audit. NOTE: event_payload may be redacted depending on caller privileges.

operations.name: at

prerequisites.description: A moderation audit entry may reference an originating report (discussion_board_reports.report_id). Ensure a report record exists because audit entries that reference reports cannot be created without a persisted report. If creating the report fails, the audit entry that references it cannot exist and the moderation audit read may be invalid for that reference.

Moderation actions are the primary source of moderation audit records (discussion_board_moderation_actions → discussion_board_moderation_audit). Create a moderation action to produce the corresponding audit entry. If this prerequisite fails, any audit entries tied to moderation_action_id will not exist.

operations.specification: This operation computes a moderation dashboard overview by aggregating data from discussion_board_reports, discussion_board_moderation_actions, and discussion_board_moderation_audit. It is a read-only computed endpoint that returns KPI metrics (pending report counts, action breakdowns, average processing times) and a short sanitized list of recent high-priority audit entries. The operation does not map to a single Prisma table but composes queries across these models to provide moderator-facing operational insights.
operations.summary: Moderation dashboard overview aggregating reports, actions, and audit metrics
operations.description:
Compute moderation overview metrics aggregated from reports, moderation actions, and moderation audit records.

Purpose and overview: Provides consolidated dashboard metrics for moderation teams: pending reports (24h/7d), counts of moderation actions by type, average time-to-first-action and time-to-resolution, and a short list of recent high-priority audit entries. The recent-items list MUST be sanitized (id, event_type, occurred_at, short_summary) to avoid leaking full event_payload in the overview context. Full payload access requires a deep-link to the audit detail endpoint with stricter access controls.

Security considerations and user permissions: Access restricted to moderator or higher roles. The endpoint must enforce RBAC and implement rate limiting and caching to avoid expensive repeated aggregations. Any inclusion of audit detail must adhere to the event_payload redaction policy.

Relationship to underlying database entities: Composes queries across discussion_board_reports (status, created_at, processed_at), discussion_board_moderation_actions (created_at, action_type), and discussion_board_moderation_audit (recent high-priority events). Implementations SHOULD paginate or limit the recent-items list.

Validation rules and business logic: No path parameters. Optional query parameters for windowing or priority can be added later (e.g., ?window=24h). Return codes: 200 with overview DTO, 401 unauthorized, 403 forbidden, 500 internal error.

responseBody.description: Aggregated moderation metrics and a sanitized short list of recent high-priority audit entries

operations.name: overview

prerequisites.description: The moderation overview aggregates report metrics (pending counts, priority). Create one or more reports so the dashboard has report data to aggregate; without persisted reports counts and prioritization will be empty or zero, preventing realistic overview results.

The moderation overview composes counts and processing-time metrics from moderation actions. Create moderation actions so the dashboard can compute action breakdowns and average processing times. If no moderation actions are created, those sections of the overview will be empty.

operations.specification: Provides rich, paginated search and retrieval of moderation reports stored in the Prisma model discussion_board_reports. This operation is read-only and is intended for moderator triage workflows. It executes complex queries against the discussion_board_reports table, optionally joining to discussion_board_member (reporterMember) and discussion_board_member_sessions (reporterSession) to provide contextual reporter information when the requesting moderator has the required audit privilege. The operation supports filtering by target_type/target_id, reason_category, status, created_at range, and derived priority signals (e.g., high reportCount for a given target). Aggregations (reportCount per target) should be computed using the discussion_board_reports table and indexed fields (target_type, target_id, created_at). Implementation MUST NOT modify report data; it only reads and aggregates. When reporterSession or reporterMember fields are included in the response, the server MUST enforce RBAC: only moderators with explicit audit privileges (e.g., permission 'moderation.audit') may receive IP or email values. Such accesses MUST be recorded in moderation audit logs.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve paginated moderation reports
operations.description:
Purpose and overview:

This operation returns a paginated, filterable list of report summaries drawn directly from the discussion_board_reports Prisma model. It is used by moderators to triage reported items (articles, comments, attachments) and to identify high-priority targets by aggregating report counts per target. The operation supports advanced filters and sorting to enable prioritized moderation workflows.

Security and user permissions:

Access to this endpoint MUST be restricted to moderator actors. Reporter session details (reporter_session_id) and raw session metadata (IP/href) MUST only be returned when the calling moderator has the explicit audit privilege (e.g., 'moderation.audit'); otherwise those fields MUST be omitted to protect reporter privacy. All accesses that return reporter session or reporter email MUST be logged in moderation audit trails and discussion_board_audit_logs.

Relationship to underlying database entities:

This operation maps to the discussion_board_reports table and uses these columns: reporter_member_id, reporter_session_id, target_type, target_id, reason_category, explanation, status, created_at, processed_at, closed_at. When reporter context is requested and permitted by RBAC, the service may join to discussion_board_member (reporterMember) and discussion_board_member_sessions (reporterSession) to include reporter display_name and session ip for triage; however email and any other PII MUST only be returned to privileged callers and must be audited.

Validation rules and business logic:

- Filters accepted in request body: targetType (string), targetId (UUID), reasonCategory (string), status (string), createdAtFrom (ISO 8601), createdAtTo (ISO 8601), priority (boolean derived via aggregation), includeProcessed (boolean), includeReporterContext (boolean - requires audit privilege).
- Sorting options: created_at (asc/desc), processed_at (asc/desc), priority (desc).
- Pagination: page, limit (server enforces a maximum limit to protect DB; recommended max limit = 100).
- Aggregation: service SHOULD compute reportCount per (target_type, target_id) and MAY include an aggregation field reportCount in the response to help moderators identify hot targets.
- Behavior: If a filter references a non-existent target_id, return an empty page rather than an error. Malformed UUIDs or dates MUST return 400 with validation details.

Related operations:

This operation is typically followed by moderator action endpoints that create discussion_board_moderation_actions and append entries to discussion_board_moderation_audit. Clients may call this endpoint to assemble the moderator queue and then call action endpoints to resolve items.

requestBody.description: Search and pagination parameters for moderation queue retrieval. Fields: targetType, targetId, reasonCategory, status, priority, createdAtFrom, createdAtTo, includeProcessed, includeReporterContext (boolean - requires audit privilege), page, limit, sortBy.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of moderation report summaries with optional reporter summary and an aggregated reportCount per target to aid prioritization. Reporter IP/email included only when caller has explicit audit privilege and such access is logged.

prerequisites.description: Create an article to serve as a reportable target (provides a targetId). The moderation queue aggregates reports by target_id, so an article must exist when testing or seeding reports that reference an article target.

Create a comment under an article to produce a comment targetId. Comments are reported independently; the comment must exist (and its parent article) before creating reports that reference a comment target.
Create attachment metadata for an article to produce an attachment targetId. Attachment records must exist before reports can reference the attachment as a target.

Create report records (discussion_board_reports) that reference a targetId (article/comment/attachment). The moderationQueue operation reads and aggregates these report records; creating reports is required to populate the moderation queue.

operations.name: index

operations.specification: Search and retrieve paginated member accounts from the discussion_board_member table. This operation is intended for privileged moderators/administrators for user-management and audit tasks, enabling filtering by username, role, mfa_enabled, created_at ranges, and optionally including soft-deleted accounts. It is read-only and must never return password_hash or other secret fields. Access to privileged fields (email, deleted_at) requires explicit RBAC and audit logging.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve paginated list of members
operations.description:
Purpose and overview:

This operation provides administrators and privileged moderators a way to search, filter, and page through member accounts stored in the discussion_board_member table. Typical uses include user investigations, export preparation for compliance, and bulk review of accounts that match suspicious patterns.

Security and user permissions:

Access that returns sensitive fields such as email or deleted_at MUST be restricted to privileged callers and MUST be audited. The endpoint MUST redact password_hash (never returned) and must limit exposure of personally-identifying information to authorized actors only. Calls that request privileged fields SHOULD be recorded in discussion_board_audit_logs for accountability.

Relationship to underlying database entities:

This operation maps to the discussion_board_member Prisma model and must reference only fields defined on that model. The Prisma model includes password_hash, but the implementation and response DTOs MUST never expose password_hash. Default summary fields returned SHOULD be: id, username, displayName, role, mfaEnabled, createdAt. Privileged optional fields (email, deleted_at) may be included only when explicitly requested by a privileged caller and when audit logging is performed.

Validation rules and business logic:

- Accepted filters in request body: username (partial match), role (exact match), mfaEnabled (boolean), createdAtFrom/To (ISO 8601), includeDeleted (boolean).
- Pagination: page, limit (server enforces a maximum limit to protect DB; recommended max limit = 100).
- Sorting: created_at (asc/desc) and username.
- Default behavior: when includeDeleted is false (default), exclude rows with deleted_at not null; when true, include them to support recovery and audit flows (deleted_at exists in schema so this is implementable).
- Error handling: malformed dates or invalid filter values MUST return 400 with field-level messages; filtering by email is allowed only for callers with elevated privileges and such accesses MUST be audited.

Related operations:

This endpoint is commonly used together with user administration endpoints (role update, suspension) and audit exports. Implementations should record admin access to member data in discussion_board_audit_logs for accountability.

requestBody.description: Search and pagination parameters for member listing. Fields: username (partial), role, mfaEnabled, createdAtFrom, createdAtTo, includeDeleted, page, limit, sortBy. Admin callers may request additional privileged fields such as email (requires audit).

responseBody.description: Paginated list of member summaries matching the search criteria. Default items include id, username, displayName, role, mfaEnabled, createdAt. For privileged callers (audited), responses may include email and deleted_at when explicitly requested.

operations.name: index

operations.specification: Retrieve public member profile by username from the discussion_board_member Prisma table. This operation queries the discussion_board_member table by the globally unique username (@@unique([username])) and returns a sanitized public summary DTO containing id, username, display_name and created_at. Sensitive fields such as password_hash, email, role and mfa_enabled are never returned. The operation responds 404 if the member does not exist or if discussion_board_member.deleted_at is not null.
operations.summary: Retrieve public member profile by username (DiscussionBoardMember)
operations.description:
Retrieve a member's public profile by their unique username. This read-only operation returns a sanitized summary view derived from the discussion_board_member table suitable for public display.

Security and permissions:
This endpoint is public and requires no authentication. The service MUST exclude sensitive fields (password_hash, email, role, mfa_enabled) from the public response. For richer, authenticated views use a separate authenticated endpoint (for example GET /me).

Database relationship and validation:
This operation reads the discussion_board_member model using the unique username index (@@unique([username])). The path parameter memberUsername is a global unique business identifier. The service MUST return 404 if the member is not found or if discussion_board_member.deleted_at is not null (soft-deleted).

Error handling:
Return 404 for not found. Return standard 5xx responses for server errors. Ensure returned timestamps are ISO 8601 (UTC).

parameters.name: memberUsername
parameters.description: Unique username of the target member (global scope)

responseBody.description: Public summary view of a DiscussionBoard member containing non-sensitive profile fields (IDiscussionBoardMember.ISummary). Fields included: id, username, display_name, created_at.

operations.name: at

operations.specification: Update an existing member's editable fields in the discussion_board_member Prisma table. This operation updates fields that are user-editable (for example display_name and password) for the member identified by the unique username. It targets the discussion_board_member table and must enforce ownership and authorization: only the authenticated member matching the username (or an elevated administrative actor) may perform the update. The operation must validate incoming data (password strength, display name length) before persisting changes and must map the incoming request DTO to the database update payload (handle password hashing in service layer).
operations.description:
Purpose and overview:
Allows a member to update their own profile information. The operation updates the discussion_board_member table row identified by the unique username path parameter. Updatable fields are limited to those appropriate for self-service: display_name and password (password should be provided as plain text in the request and must be hashed before persisting into password_hash). Username and email changes are out-of-scope for this endpoint unless explicitly permitted by policy and additional verification.

Security and authorization:
This endpoint requires authentication and enforces ownership checks: the authenticated actor must represent the member identified by {memberUsername} or possess administrative privileges. The implementation must verify the caller's identity (session or JWT) and deny updates if the actor is not the owner and not an administrator. When a password change is requested, the service must validate password strength (business rule: minimum 12 characters and at least three categories among uppercase, lowercase, number, symbol) and then hash the password using the configured hashing algorithm. After a successful password change the service should revoke active sessions per security policy.

Relationship to DB entity and validation rules:
This operation updates the discussion_board_member model. Validate that the target member exists and is not soft-deleted (deleted_at is null) before applying changes. The request payload maps to IDiscussionBoardMember.IUpdate; implementation must not allow direct writes to password_hash or created_at/updated_at/deleted_at fields from the client. All changes must update updated_at timestamp and return the updated resource representation.

Related operations and behavior:
Clients should call GET /members/{memberUsername} to retrieve public profile before updating. For self-profile queries use GET /me which returns private fields. On success return the updated member resource representation; on authorization failure return 403; on not-found return 404.
operations.summary: Update a member's profile (self-service)

parameters.name: memberUsername
parameters.description: Unique username of the target member (global scope)

requestBody.description: Editable member fields. The request maps to IDiscussionBoardMember.IUpdate and typically includes 'displayName' and optionally 'password' for password change. Password must meet strength rules and will be hashed server-side.

responseBody.description: Updated member resource representation (IDiscussionBoardMember) returned after successful update

operations.name: update

operations.specification: Update an existing member's editable fields on the discussion_board_member Prisma table. This operation updates user-editable fields (display_name and optionally password) for the member identified by the globally unique username. Ownership and authorization must be enforced: only the authenticated member matching the username or an elevated administrator may perform the update. Passwords in the request are plaintext and MUST be validated for strength and hashed server-side before persisting into password_hash. On password change, revoke active sessions per security policy and record an audit entry. The operation must not permit client writes to protected fields (created_at, updated_at, deleted_at, password_hash).
operations.summary: Update a member's profile (self-service)
operations.description:
Allows a member to update their own profile information. The operation updates the discussion_board_member record identified by the unique username path parameter. Updatable fields are limited to display_name and password. Passwords are supplied in plaintext in the request, MUST be validated for strength (minimum 12 characters and at least three categories among uppercase, lowercase, number, symbol), and MUST be hashed server-side before persisting to password_hash. The service MUST NOT accept password_hash or allow clients to set created_at/updated_at/deleted_at.

Security and authorization:
This endpoint requires authentication and enforces ownership: the authenticated actor must be the member identified by {memberUsername} or possess administrative privileges. If the caller is not authorized, return 403. On successful password change, revoke active refresh tokens per security policy and write an audit log entry (without including raw passwords).

Database relationship and validation:

- Prisma model: discussion_board_member (schema provided).
- Identifier chosen: discussion_board_member.username (schema-enforced unique field, @@unique([username])).
- Soft-delete column: discussion_board_member.deleted_at (DateTime?). The schema includes deleted_at, so the operation implements soft-delete semantics rather than physical row removal.

The endpoint MUST not disclose `password_hash` or other sensitive moderator fields in responses.

If the moderator already has `deleted_at` set, return 409 Conflict. On success, set `deleted_at` to now, revoke active sessions, create `discussion_board_moderation_actions` with `action_type='remove'` and a `discussion_board_moderation_audit` entry, and record a system audit log entry. The operation accepts the polymorphic target (target_type + target_id) and delivery preferences (delivery_mode, active). The Prisma schema enforces uniqueness over (discussion_board_member_id, target_type, target_id) so implementations must check for existing non-deleted subscriptions and return 409 Conflict or return the existing subscription for idempotent behavior. The implementation must populate created_at and updated_at timestamps and set deleted_at to null on creation.
operations.summary: Create a subscription for a member to a target (discussion_board_subscriptions)
operations.description:
Purpose and overview:

Create a subscription linking the named member to a specific target (an article or an author). This operation writes to the discussion_board_subscriptions Prisma table and accepts a request body describing the polymorphic target (target_type, target_id) and delivery preferences (delivery_mode, active). The Prisma schema includes a uniqueness constraint on (discussion_board_member_id, target_type, target_id) so the implementation must enforce idempotency or return a 409 Conflict when attempting to create a duplicate subscription.

Security and permissions:

This endpoint requires an authenticated actor. The implementation MUST verify that the caller corresponds to {memberUsername} or is a moderator (authorizationActors: ["member","moderator"]). Unauthorized callers must receive 403.

Validation rules and business logic:

- Validate that memberUsername exists; return 404 if not.
- Validate target_type against allowed subscription types (e.g., "article","author"); return 400 for unsupported values.
- Validate target_id is a UUID and that the referenced resource exists when applicable (e.g., article exists if target_type == "article"); return 404 if the referenced resource does not exist.
- Reject creation with 409 Conflict if a non-deleted subscription already exists for the same (member, target_type, target_id). Optionally return the existing subscription to support idempotency.
- The request body MUST NOT include the member identifier; the member is provided in the path and any member id in the body must be ignored.

Side effects and auditing:

- On success, worker processes may update subscription caches or enqueue notifications. The creation event should be recorded in moderation/audit logs per audit policy.

Responses and errors:

- 201: subscription created successfully (response body: IDiscussionBoardSubscription)
- 400: validation error (invalid targetType, invalid UUID, missing required fields)
- 401: unauthenticated
- 403: caller not authorized
- 404: member not found or referenced target resource not found
- 409: conflict - duplicate subscription exists
- 500: internal error

parameters.name: memberUsername
parameters.description: Unique username of the member creating the subscription (global scope)

requestBody.description: Subscription creation payload. Do not repeat the member identifier in the body; the member is identified by the path parameter {memberUsername}. Fields include: target_type (string), target_id (uuid), delivery_mode (string: e.g., 'immediate'|'daily_digest'), active (boolean).

responseBody.description: The created subscription record as stored in the discussion_board_subscriptions table.

prerequisites.description: When creating a subscription with target_type = 'article', the referenced article (target_id) must already exist. Use POST /discussionBoard/member/articles to create the article and obtain a valid target_id before calling the subscription creation endpoint. If the article does not exist, creating the subscription should fail with 404 (referenced target not found).

operations.name: create

operations.specification: Upsert member subscription record into discussion_board_subscriptions table. This operation targets the Prisma model `discussion_board_subscriptions` and implements idempotent PUT semantics to create or update a subscription that links a member to a polymorphic target (target_type + target_id). The server must resolve memberUsername -> discussion_board_member.id and validate target existence (e.g., article id exists for target_type='article' or member id exists for target_type='author') before persisting. This operation uses transactional upsert semantics to enforce the model-level unique constraint (discussion_board_member_id, target_type, target_id).
operations.summary: Create or update a member subscription to a target (discussion_board_subscriptions)
operations.description:
Create or replace a subscription for the specified member to a target resource.

This endpoint maps to the Prisma model `discussion_board_subscriptions`. It allows a member to subscribe to a target (for example, an article or an author) and select a delivery preference. The operation performs an idempotent upsert: create a new subscription row when none exists, or update delivery preferences and active flag when a row already exists.

Security: Only the authenticated member identified by `{memberUsername}` (or an administrator) may create or modify their subscriptions. The implementation MUST resolve `memberUsername` to the member UUID (discussion_board_member.id) and verify the request actor (JWT) matches that member or has admin privileges.

Validation rules and error handling: 400 Bad Request for invalid targetType/targetId or delivery_mode; 401/403 for auth failures; 201 Created for new subscription, 200 OK for update.

parameters.name: memberUsername
parameters.description: Unique username of the member (corresponds to discussion_board_member.username; global scope)

parameters.name: targetType
parameters.description: Polymorphic subscription target type (e.g., 'article' or 'author'). The server validates this value and resolves target_id accordingly.

parameters.name: targetId
parameters.description: UUID of the target resource identified by targetType (e.g., discussion_board_articles.id for 'article' or discussion_board_member.id for 'author').

requestBody.description: Subscription creation payload. Contains delivery preference and active flag. Path parameters supply memberUsername, targetType and targetId and MUST NOT be duplicated here.

responseBody.description: Created or updated subscription record reflecting persisted fields in discussion_board_subscriptions.

operations.name: update

prerequisites.description: If the subscription target is an article (targetType = 'article'), the article must exist before upserting the subscription. Use POST /discussionBoard/member/articles to create the article and obtain the required targetId. If article creation fails or the article does not exist, the upsert cannot succeed and should return 404/400 accordingly.

operations.specification: Soft-delete (deactivate) a member subscription in discussion_board_subscriptions. This operation implements the business unsubscribe semantics on the Prisma model `discussion_board_subscriptions` by marking the row as deleted (setting deleted_at) and setting active=false so the subscription is excluded from delivery flows while preserved for audit.
operations.summary: Unsubscribe (soft-delete) a member subscription
operations.description:
Deactivate (soft-delete) a subscription for the specified member to a target resource. The endpoint locates the subscription by the resolved member id and the (targetType, targetId) tuple and marks it as deleted (deleted_at) and inactive (active=false).

This operation preserves an audit trail and is idempotent: attempting to unsubscribe an already-deleted subscription returns success (204 No Content).

Security: Only the authenticated member identified by `{memberUsername}` or an administrator may perform this action. The server MUST verify authentication and ownership (or admin privileges).

parameters.name: memberUsername
parameters.description: Unique username of the member (corresponds to discussion_board_member.username; global scope)

parameters.name: targetType
parameters.description: Polymorphic subscription target type (e.g., 'article' or 'author'). The server validates this value and resolves target_id accordingly.

parameters.name: targetId
parameters.description: UUID of the target resource identified by targetType (e.g., discussion_board_articles.id for 'article' or discussion_board_member.id for 'author').

operations.name: erase
