Creating a subscription (POST /discussionBoard/member/members/{memberUsername}/subscriptions) ensures a discussion_board_subscriptions row exists for the member and the (targetType, targetId) tuple; if this prerequisite fails the unsubscribe operation cannot locate or deactivate the subscription.

operations.specification: Manage and search member notifications stored in the discussion_board_notifications table. This operation implements a paginated search and optional bulk update/marking interface for notifications belonging to a specific member. It operates on the discussion_board_notifications table from the Prisma schema and leverages related tables such as discussion_board_subscriptions and discussion_board_articles to filter or enrich results. The request payload uses IDiscussionBoardNotification.IRequest to express complex search, filter, pagination and bulk action parameters. The response returns a paginated summary view IPageIDiscussionBoardNotification.ISummary suitable for list displays.
operations.summary: Search and bulk-manage notifications for a member
operations.description:
Retrieve and perform bulk operations on a member's notifications. This operation provides advanced search, filtering, sorting and bulk mutation capabilities for notifications tied to a member. It is implemented against the discussion_board_notifications table as defined in the Prisma schema and returns paginated summary entries optimized for list displays.

Security and permissions: This endpoint requires authentication and that the authenticated actor either be the member identified by {memberUsername} or have appropriate administrative privileges. Server-side logic MUST verify member ownership by resolving the provided username to discussion_board_member.id and matching notifications by discussion_board_notifications.recipient_member_id. Audit-write actions (bulk modifications) SHOULD create appropriate audit entries in discussion_board_audit_logs. For list results the ISummary type SHOULD NOT include full `payload` content to avoid accidental PII exposure; include only sanitized excerpt or a hasPayload flag in the summary.

parameters.name: memberUsername
parameters.description: Unique username of the target member (global scope)

requestBody.description: Search filters, pagination parameters and optional bulk actions to perform on the matched notifications (IDiscussionBoardNotification.IRequest)

responseBody.description: Paginated list of notification summaries matching search criteria and the result of any requested bulk operation

prerequisites.description: The referenced article must exist before notifications can reference or filter by articleId. Creating the article (POST /discussionBoard/member/articles) ensures discussion_board_articles.id is available for notification filtering/enrichment; without it notification queries referencing articleId may be invalid.

The subscription must exist when filtering or performing bulk actions scoped by subscriptionId. Creating the subscription (POST /discussionBoard/member/members/{memberUsername}/subscriptions) ensures a discussion_board_subscriptions row exists for the member and target so notifications can be properly matched and bulk-updated. If this prerequisite fails, subscription-scoped notification operations cannot proceed.

operations.name: index

operations.specification: Retrieve a single member notification by id from the discussion_board_notifications table. This operation returns the complete notification record for a given member and notification id. It maps directly to the discussion_board_notifications table and returns IDiscussionBoardNotification DTO for successful responses. Access is restricted to the notification recipient or authorized administrators and moderator access MUST be audited.
operations.summary: Get a single notification for a member
operations.description:
Return full details for a single notification belonging to the specified member. The response contains the complete notification record as defined by the discussion_board_notifications table and is intended to support a notification detail view in the client UI.

Security: The endpoint requires authentication. The authenticated actor must be the member identified by {memberUsername} or an administrator. Ownership is enforced by matching notification.recipient_member_id to the member id resolved from the username. Access by moderators/administrators should be logged for audit purposes. Full `payload` content should be returned only to authorized callers (recipient or admin) and otherwise redacted.

parameters.name: memberUsername
parameters.description: Unique username of the target member (global scope)

parameters.name: notificationId
parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the notification

responseBody.description: Detailed notification information for the specified member and notification id

operations.name: at

operations.specification: Retrieve a filtered, paginated list of delivery failure records for a single notification. This operation is implemented against the Prisma model discussion_board_notification_failures and is scoped by the parent discussion_board_notifications record (discussion_board_notification_id). It supports filtering by attempt number ranges, attempted_at and created_at date ranges, exact error_code matching, and full-text search on error_message. Results are paginated and sorted and returned as summary DTOs for diagnostic listing. The operation validates that the notification belongs to the member identified by discussion_board_member.username (memberUsername) or that the caller holds elevated privileges; it relies on the database relationship discussion_board_notifications.recipient_member_id -> discussion_board_member.id for ownership verification.
operations.summary: List delivery failure records for a member's notification
operations.description:
Purpose and overview:

Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of delivery failure records related to a single notification (discussion_board_notifications) for the specified member. Each returned item maps to a row in the discussion_board_notification_failures table and contains the attempt_number, attempted_at, error_code, error_message, backoff_until and created_at fields. This endpoint is intended for diagnostics by the member or support staff to inspect why a notification delivery failed.

Security and permissions:

Only the member who owns the notification (identified by memberUsername) or an authorized support/administrator role should be allowed to inspect these failure records. The controller must verify that the notification (discussion_board_notifications.id) is associated with the member (discussion_board_notifications.recipient_member_id -> discussion_board_member.id) that matches the provided memberUsername, or that the caller holds appropriate elevated privileges. JWT-based authentication and role checks are expected to be enforced by the API layer.

Relationship to database entities:

This operation queries discussion_board_notification_failures with discussion_board_notification_id equal to the notificationId path parameter. Use the composite unique constraint @@unique([discussion_board_notification_id, attempt_number]) for deterministic single-attempt lookup when applicable. Returned items are transformed into IDiscussionBoardNotificationFailure.ISummary DTOs optimized for list displays.

Validation rules and business logic:

- Validate that memberUsername corresponds to an existing discussion_board_member.username (global unique username). Use the username for path identification per parameter selection priority.
- Validate notificationId is a UUID and that the referenced discussion_board_notifications exists and is owned by the memberUsername.
- Request filters MUST NOT include path-identifying fields (notificationId or memberUsername).
- Support pagination (page, limit), sorting by attempted_at or created_at, and full-text search on error_message. Enforce a maximum page size (e.g., 100) to mitigate abusive queries.

Responses and errors:

- 200: IPageIDiscussionBoardNotificationFailure.ISummary — paginated summary of failure records
- 400: Invalid request body or filter parameters
- 401/403: Unauthorized if the caller is not the owner nor authorized support/admin
- 404: notificationId not found or not associated with memberUsername

Related operations:

- GET /members/{memberUsername}/notifications/{notificationId}/failures/{attemptNumber} — retrieves a single failure entry by attempt number for the same notification
- GET /members/{memberUsername}/notifications/{notificationId} — retrieve notification metadata

parameters.name: memberUsername
parameters.description: Unique username of the target member (global scope)

parameters.name: notificationId
parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the target notification (discussion_board_notifications.id)

requestBody.description: Search, filtering and pagination parameters for notification failure records scoped to the notificationId. Fields include page (int), limit (int), sort (string, e.g., 'attempted_at' or '-attempted_at'), attemptNumberFrom (int), attemptNumberTo (int), attemptedAtFrom (string, date-time), attemptedAtTo (string, date-time), createdAtFrom (string, date-time), createdAtTo (string, date-time), errorCode (string), errorMessageQuery (string for full-text search).

responseBody.description: Paginated list of notification failure summary records for the specified notification.

operations.name: index

operations.specification: Retrieve a single delivery failure record for a specific attempt number of a notification. This operation reads the discussion_board_notification_failures table and leverages the composite uniqueness constraint (discussion_board_notification_id + attempt_number) to identify a single failure row. It returns detailed diagnostic fields including id, discussion_board_notification_id, attempt_number, attempted_at, error_code, error_message, backoff_until, and created_at.
operations.summary: Get a specific delivery failure entry for a notification
operations.description:
Purpose and overview:

Return the detailed delivery failure record for a specific attempt (attemptNumber) of a given notification. Useful for members or support staff to view the exact error and timing captured in discussion_board_notification_failures for one delivery attempt.

Security and permissions:

Access is restricted to the member owning the notification (memberUsername) or authorized support/administration roles. The controller must verify ownership by resolving discussion_board_notifications.recipient_member_id to the discussion_board_member record matching memberUsername, or validate the caller's elevated privileges.

Relationship to database entities:

This operation reads from discussion_board_notification_failures and uses the composite unique constraint @@unique([discussion_board_notification_id, attempt_number]) to retrieve a single deterministic row. The returned DTO is IDiscussionBoardNotificationFailure and should include the persistent fields: id, discussion_board_notification_id, attempt_number, attempted_at, error_code, error_message, backoff_until, created_at.

Validation rules and business logic:

- Validate memberUsername exists and is the owner of the notification referenced by notificationId.
- Validate notificationId is a UUID and exists.
- Validate attemptNumber is an integer (non-negative) and that a corresponding failure record exists for the composite key (notificationId, attemptNumber).
- Redact or withhold internal-only diagnostic payloads unless the caller has ADMIN/support privileges; expose error_code and error_message to owners for transparency.

Responses and errors:

- 200: IDiscussionBoardNotificationFailure — detailed failure record
- 400: Invalid attemptNumber format or request
- 401/403: Unauthorized if caller lacks ownership or privileges
- 404: No failure record for the given composite key or notification not associated with the memberUsername

parameters.name: memberUsername
parameters.description: Unique username of the target member (global scope)

parameters.name: notificationId
parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the target notification (discussion_board_notifications.id)

parameters.name: attemptNumber
parameters.description: Sequential attempt number of the notification failure scoped to the notification

responseBody.description: Detailed notification failure record containing attempt_number, attempted_at, error_code, error_message, backoff_until, and created_at.

a standard format for JWT-based authentication across the generated backend
applications.

IDiscussionBoardGuest.ICreate.description: Create DTO for registering a temporary guest identity. This request creates a row in the `discussion_board_guest` table and (server-side) issues short-lived credentials. Session-context fields are required for self-join flows and must be provided by the client.

displayName.description: Optional display name supplied by the guest for short-lived attribution. Maps to Prisma `display_name` when persisted. Nullable.

IDiscussionBoardGuest.IAuthorized.description:
Authorized response for guest authentication/refresh operations. Contains the guest id and issued tokens. Maps to Prisma model discussion_board_guest.

Notes on sensitive fields and usage:
- The `ip` field is considered PII. API implementations MUST redact or return null for `ip` unless the caller has explicit audit/trace privileges. Returning `ip` to unprivileged callers is a security risk.
- The `guest` property is an optional convenience summary (IDiscussionBoardGuest.ISummary). It is included only when the server chooses to embed a snapshot to avoid an extra user-info lookup. Do NOT treat `guest` as required; canonical identification uses the top-level `id` field.

Naming guidance:
- This schema has been normalized to use camelCase property names (createdAt/updatedAt/deletedAt/displayName) for consistency with the rest of the API surface.

id.description: Unique identifier of the authenticated guest (discussion_board_guest.id).

displayName.description: Optional display name supplied by the guest. May be null if not provided.

ip.description: Observed IP address for the guest session. CONTAINS PII: must be redacted (set to null) for callers without audit/trace privileges.

createdAt.description: Record creation timestamp in ISO 8601 UTC (discussion_board_guest.created_at).

updatedAt.description: Record last-update timestamp in ISO 8601 UTC (discussion_board_guest.updated_at).

deletedAt.description: Soft-delete timestamp (discussion_board_guest.deleted_at). Null indicates active record.

guest.description: Optional guest summary metadata for client convenience. Nullable/omitted when not provided by the server.

IDiscussionBoardGuest.IRefresh.description:
Request body to refresh guest credentials. The refresh token is validated and the referenced discussion_board_guest row MUST be checked for existence and non-deleted state before issuing new credentials.

Implementation notes:
- `refresh_token` is an opaque bearer token. The server MUST validate token integrity and mapping to an active discussion_board_guest record. If the referenced guest row has deleted_at set, the server SHOULD reject renewal and require a new join.
- Naming: this schema uses `refresh_token` (snake_case) intentionally to align with common refresh-request payloads. The property remains required and the server may normalize or map token names when producing camelCase client SDKs.

refresh_token.description: Opaque refresh token previously issued by the auth service. The server validates this token and ensures the referenced discussion_board_guest row exists and deleted_at is null (or within retention policy) before issuing new credentials.

This lightweight summary is intended for embedding in lists and references where minimal guest context is required (id, optional display name, and creation time). Fields are drawn directly from the Prisma model comments and reflect persisted columns.

id.description: Primary key (UUID) of the guest record (discussion_board_guest.id).

display_name.description: Optional display name supplied by the guest. Nullable when the guest did not provide a display name.

created_at.description: Record creation timestamp (ISO 8601 UTC) from discussion_board_guest.created_at.

updated_at.description: Record last-update timestamp in ISO 8601 UTC (discussion_board_guest.updated_at).

IDiscussionBoardMember.ISummary.description: Public summary of a member suitable for embedding in search results and lists. Maps to Prisma model discussion_board_member and excludes sensitive fields. Includes creation timestamp for consistent embedding across DTOs.

display_name.description: Optional public display name; may be null if not set.

created_at.description: Account creation timestamp (ISO 8601 UTC). Maps to discussion_board_member.created_at in Prisma.

IDiscussionBoardMember.IJoin.description: Member registration (self sign-up) DTO. Plain-text password is accepted and MUST be hashed by the server before persisting to discussion_board_member.password_hash. The server MUST also create an email verification record (discussion_board_email_verifications) with a single-use token that expires in 48 hours, set the persisted role to the application default (e.g., "USER") if not otherwise configured, and set mfa_enabled = false by default. Uniqueness constraints on username and email are enforced by the database; the API returns 409 Conflict on violations. Session context fields (href, referrer) are required for creating an initial session record. Clients MUST NOT supply server-managed fields such as id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at, role, password_hash, or mfa_enabled.

username.description: Chosen username (unique). 3-30 characters. Allowed characters: letters, numbers, underscore, dot, hyphen. Server will normalize/validate uniqueness (409 on conflict).

email.description: Verified email address for account and notification delivery. The server will create a single-use verification token and send a verification email; do NOT treat presence of email as proof the address is verified.

password.description: Plain-text password. The server MUST hash this value before storing it in discussion_board_member.password_hash. Minimum 12 characters and must include at least three of the following categories: uppercase letter, lowercase letter, number, symbol. Clients MUST NOT send pre-hashed values.

ip.description: Optional client IP address for session context (server may extract it if omitted). Treated as sensitive PII; server MAY redact this in responses for non-privileged callers.

href.description: Connection URL (current page URL) - mandatory for session context when creating an initial session record.

referrer.description: Referrer URL (previous page URL) - mandatory for session context when creating an initial session record.

IDiscussionBoardMember.IAuthorized.description: Authorized response returned after successful authentication or refresh. This response is intended for authenticated contexts only and includes JWT tokens and member metadata. `email` is included because this is an authorized response (sensitive); clients that need a reduced public view should call GET /me or use the member summary. The `member` property is a lightweight summary; use GET /me for full profile. Note: IAuthorizationToken uses snake_case property names (access, refresh, expired_at, refreshable_until); client SDKs may need to normalize token property casing for language idioms.

username.description: Unique username chosen by the member (discussion_board_member.username).

email.description: Verified email address for the member. Included only in authorized responses; treat as sensitive.

role.description: Actor role identifier (e.g., 'USER', 'ADMIN'). Stored in the database as discussion_board_member.role.

mfa_enabled.description: Whether the member has enabled multi-factor authentication (discussion_board_member.mfa_enabled).

created_at.description: Record creation timestamp (UTC) from the Prisma model (discussion_board_member.created_at).

updated_at.description: Record last modification timestamp (UTC) from the Prisma model (discussion_board_member.updated_at).

deleted_at.description: Soft-delete timestamp if the account is soft-deleted (discussion_board_member.deleted_at). Nullable.

member.description: Lightweight member summary included for client convenience. Use GET /me for full profile when needed.

usernameOrEmail.description: The member's username or email address used to authenticate. The authentication flow will match this value against discussion_board_member.username or discussion_board_member.email.

password.description: Plain-text password supplied for authentication. MUST be transmitted over TLS. The server is responsible for verifying against discussion_board_member.password_hash; the password MUST NOT be returned in any response.

ip.description: Optional client IP address for session context. Server may extract automatically; clients MAY supply it for SSR or special cases. Nullable.

href.description: Optional connection URL (current page URL). When provided, the server records session context in discussion_board_member_sessions.href. Not required for basic login payloads.

referrer.description: Optional referrer URL (previous page URL). When provided, the server records session context in discussion_board_member_sessions.referrer. Not required for basic login payloads.

IDiscussionBoardMember.ILogin.description: Login request for members. Includes credentials and optional session context fields (href, referrer). 'ip' is optional and may be null. Do NOT include member identifiers (member ids) in this payload; the server derives the authenticated member identity upon success.

IDiscussionBoardMember.description: Sanitized public member response DTO. Mirrors non-sensitive persisted columns from discussion_board_member in Prisma. Omits credential fields (password_hash). Includes membership metadata required by consumers. Timestamps use ISO 8601 (UTC).

id.description: Unique identifier of the member (Prisma: discussion_board_member.id).

username.description: Unique username chosen by the member (Prisma: discussion_board_member.username).

display_name.description: Optional public display name (Prisma: discussion_board_member.display_name). Nullable when the member did not set a display name or was anonymized.

role.description: Actor role identifier for the member (Prisma: discussion_board_member.role). Examples: 'USER', 'ADMIN'. Included for authorized contexts; use for RBAC decisions in UI and client logic.

mfa_enabled.description: Whether the member has enabled multi-factor authentication (Prisma: discussion_board_member.mfa_enabled). When true, login flows require step-up verification per product policy.

created_at.description: Account creation timestamp (ISO 8601 UTC) (Prisma: discussion_board_member.created_at).

updated_at.description: Last modification timestamp (ISO 8601 UTC) for the member record (Prisma: discussion_board_member.updated_at).

deleted_at.description: Soft-delete timestamp if the account is soft-deleted (Prisma: discussion_board_member.deleted_at). Nullable; presence indicates account is in soft-deleted state and may be hidden from public listings.

IDiscussionBoardMember.IRefresh.description:
Request model for token refresh. Exactly one of the alternatives MUST be provided: either the refresh-token variant (type = 'refresh_token') or the session-id variant (type = 'session_id').

The `type` discriminator is REQUIRED and MUST be an exact literal matching one of the mapped values. Implementations MUST validate the supplied variant according to the chosen discriminator: when `type` == 'refresh_token' the request MUST include `refresh_token` (opaque string) and the server MUST validate token integrity and mapping to an active discussion_board_member record and session state; when `type` == 'session_id' the request MUST include `session_id` (UUID) and the server MUST validate the referenced discussion_board_member_sessions row (expired_at, existence, deleted member). Token/session consumption and rotation semantics are server-side responsibilities and SHOULD be logged for audit.

Examples:
- Refresh token variant:
  { "type": "refresh_token", "refresh_token": "eyJhbGciOiJI...example-refresh-token" }
- Session id variant:
  { "type": "session_id", "session_id": "8a23f1e6-3b4a-4f1a-9d2b-7c1e9f0a1b23" }

IDiscussionBoardMember.IVerifyEmail.description:
Request body to verify a member's email using a single-use verification token persisted in discussion_board_email_verifications. The token is a bearer credential sent to the member's email and MUST be consumed atomically by the server (set consumed_at on first successful use). The server MUST validate the token exists, is unconsumed (consumed_at is null) and not expired (expires_at >= now) before marking the associated discussion_board_member as verified. Implementations MUST guard against race conditions (atomic consume) and SHOULD rate-limit resend attempts.

Error handling guidance for implementers: return 400 for malformed requests, 404 or 410 for unknown/expired tokens (avoid disclosing account existence where appropriate), and 409 if token appears already consumed (or return 200 with idempotent semantics depending on product policy).

token.description: Single-use verification token issued to the member's email (maps to discussion_board_email_verifications.token). Treated as a bearer credential; server MUST validate existence, expiry and single-use semantics.

IDiscussionBoardMember.IRequestPasswordR.description: Request body to initiate a password reset. Caller MUST supply at least one identifier: either 'email' (preferred) or 'username'. The server will create a discussion_board_password_resets record (token, request_ip, created_at, expires_at). Implementations MUST NOT disclose account existence in responses and SHOULD apply rate limiting (e.g., max resend attempts per hour) to prevent enumeration/abuse. Optional session/context fields (ip, href, referrer) may be provided by the client to populate discussion_board_password_resets.request_ip and session metadata for audit and anomaly detection. When provided and returned later in audit contexts, these fields contain PII and must be redacted for unprivileged callers.

IDiscussionBoardMember.IResetPassword.description: Request DTO for consuming a single-use password reset token and setting a new password. The server will validate the token against discussion_board_password_resets, ensure it is unconsumed and not expired, atomically set consumed_at, and update the member's password_hash. Do NOT include member identifiers in the request; the token is the bearer credential for this operation. Security: password strength policy applies (minimum 12 characters and at least three of: uppercase, lowercase, number, symbol). After successful reset the server SHOULD revoke existing refresh sessions; the optional revokeSessions flag lets the client request explicit revocation but servers MAY revoke by default for security.

token.description: Single-use password reset token issued via email (maps to discussion_board_password_resets.token). Treated as a bearer credential; server locates the reset record by this token and must verify expires_at and consumed_at atomically.

password.description: New plain-text password. Minimum 12 characters. The server MUST enforce additional complexity rules (at least three character classes among: uppercase, lowercase, digits, symbols) and MUST hash the password before storing it in discussion_board_member.password_hash. Clients MUST NOT send pre-hashed values.

revokeSessions.description: Optional flag; when true the server SHOULD revoke existing refresh sessions for the member after a successful reset (recommended for security). If omitted the server SHOULD revoke sessions by default as part of secure reset handling.

IDiscussionBoardMember.IChangePassword.description: Protected request DTO for authenticated members to change their own password. Used by PUT /auth/member/password/change. The caller is authenticated as the member (authorizationActor: 'member'); do NOT accept or require a member_id in the body. The server MUST verify the provided current password against discussion_board_member.password_hash before updating the stored hash. The server MUST enforce password policy (minimum 12 characters and at least three of the following categories: uppercase, lowercase, number, symbol). The implementation MUST hash the new password before persisting into discussion_board_member.password_hash, MUST update discussion_board_member.updated_at, and SHOULD record an audit entry in discussion_board_audit_logs. When revokeSessions is true the server SHOULD revoke/expire active refresh credentials and update discussion_board_member_sessions.expired_at for active sessions. Always transmit these fields over TLS. The server MUST NOT return password or password_hash in any response.

currentPassword.description: The member's current plain-text password used to authenticate the change operation. Server MUST validate this value against discussion_board_member.password_hash. Plain-text only; clients MUST NOT send pre-hashed values (e.g., 'password_hash', 'password_hashed', 'hashed_password' are forbidden). Transmit only over TLS.

newPassword.description: The new plain-text password. The server MUST enforce password policy: minimum 12 characters and at least three of the following categories: uppercase letter, lowercase letter, number, symbol. The server MUST hash this value before storing it in discussion_board_member.password_hash and MUST NOT return password or password_hash in any response. Note: implementers may apply additional complexity checks or entropy checks server-side.

revokeSessions.description: Optional flag indicating whether the server should revoke all active sessions/refresh tokens for the member after a successful password change. When true the server SHOULD expire discussion_board_member_sessions.expired_at for active sessions or otherwise revoke refresh credentials. Default when omitted: false.

IDiscussionBoardMember.IEnableTwoFactor.description: Request body to initiate/enroll two-factor authentication for the authenticated member. The server will perform enrollment steps and MUST NOT accept or require member id (actor is taken from JWT). The server MUST NOT return persistent secrets (TOTP shared secret) in API responses; any enrollment secret MUST be stored securely server-side and only exposed as a time-limited provisioning artifact (provisioning URI or QR). Recommended server behavior: return a time-limited provisioning artifact (QR SVG or provisioning URI) and require a subsequent verification step to confirm the TOTP code before permanently setting discussion_board_member.mfa_enabled = true. Alternatively, if the endpoint both issues the artifact and sets an enrolled flag, document that the server will still require a verification step during the first login. Enrollment events SHOULD be recorded in discussion_board_audit_logs. Implementations MUST require recent authentication for this operation (step-up) when sessions are stale.

method.description: Requested enrollment method. Server currently supports the exact literal 'totp'. Clients MUST use the exact value 'totp'.

return_qr_svg.description: When true, request the server return a QR code representation (SVG) as part of the enrollment artifact. If omitted or false, the server may return an alternate provisioning artifact such as a time-limited provisioning URI. Any returned artifact is time-limited and MUST NOT expose persistent secrets.

IDiscussionBoardMember.ISession.description: Session summary for a member (discussion_board_member_sessions). Returned fields are safe metadata for the actor to review sessions; do not include tokens or secret values. All timestamps use ISO 8601 'date-time' format. IP is considered PII and may be redacted (returned as null) for callers without audit/trace privileges; when redacted the property MUST still be present with explicit null.

id.description: Session record id (discussion_board_member_sessions.id). Unique UUID assigned to the session record.

memberId.description: Member foreign key referencing discussion_board_member.id. Present to indicate the owning member for the session; the server validates this relation when creating sessions.

ip.description: Client IP address observed for the session. This field contains PII and the server MAY redact it (return explicit null) for callers without audit/trace privileges. When present, return the observed IP string; when redacted return null explicitly (do not omit the property).

href.description: Connection URL (href) captured for the session (the page URL or resource path). Stored in the DB column href and returned as-is. May be long (DB VarChar(80000)).

referrer.description: Referrer URL captured for the session. May be returned as null if not available or redacted by policy.

createdAt.description: Session creation timestamp (ISO 8601 UTC). Maps to discussion_board_member_sessions.created_at in Prisma.

expiredAt.description: Session expiry time (ISO 8601 UTC). Null when session is open-ended until revoked. Maps to discussion_board_member_sessions.expired_at.

IDiscussionBoardMember.ISessionsPage.description: Paginated response containing session summaries for the authenticated member. Intended for the `member` actor (authorizationActor: 'member') to review active sessions and revoke them if necessary. Each `data` item is an IDiscussionBoardMember.ISession object representing a discussion_board_member_sessions row (fields: id, discussion_board_member_id, ip, href, referrer, created_at, expired_at). NOTE: `ip` is considered PII and may be redacted (set to null) for callers without audit/trace privileges; implementations SHOULD document redaction behavior. Servers MAY omit or set discussion_board_member_id to null in contexts where the member id is redundant (the authenticated principal is already known).

pagination.description: Pagination information (current page, limit, total records, total pages).

data.description: Array of session summaries belonging to the authenticated member. Items include session id, ip (PII), href, referrer, created_at and expired_at.

v0.summary: Typical response for member's session listing

IDiscussionBoardModerator.ICreate.description: Create DTO for a new moderator account. Maps to the Prisma model `discussion_board_moderator`. The server MUST hash the provided plain-text `password` and persist the result to `password_hash`; the plain-text password MUST NOT be stored or returned. The server MUST validate uniqueness of `username` and `email` and return 409 Conflict on duplicates. Required session context fields `href` and `referrer` are used to record an initial moderator session (discussion_board_moderator_sessions). `ip` is optional and considered PII; servers may infer from the connection when omitted. Password policy: minimum 12 characters and at least three of the following categories: uppercase, lowercase, number, symbol. Do not include server-managed fields (id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at, password_hash) in the request.

email.description: Moderator contact email. Must be unique and is used for verification and notifications.

password.description: Plain-text password. Server MUST hash this value and store the result in discussion_board_moderator.password_hash. Must meet complexity rules: minimum 12 characters and at least three character classes (uppercase, lowercase, digit, symbol).

display_name.description: Optional display name shown in moderator-facing UIs and audit entries. Nullable.

ip.description: Optional client IP address. Considered PII and may be redacted in responses to non-privileged callers.

href.description: Connection URL (current page URL). REQUIRED for self-join operations so that the server can record session context in discussion_board_moderator_sessions.href.

referrer.description: Referrer URL (previous page URL). REQUIRED for self-join operations so that the server can record session context in discussion_board_moderator_sessions.referrer.

IDiscussionBoardModerator.ISummary.description: Moderator summary used for embedding in audit records and moderation responses. Maps to the Prisma model discussion_board_moderator. Sensitive fields are excluded.

display_name.description: Optional moderator display name used in audit notes. Nullable when not set.

created_at.description: Record creation timestamp (ISO 8601 UTC). Maps to discussion_board_moderator.created_at.

updated_at.description: Record last modification timestamp (ISO 8601 UTC). Maps to discussion_board_moderator.updated_at.

deleted_at.description: Soft-delete timestamp (discussion_board_moderator.deleted_at). Null indicates active record. Returned so callers can detect soft-deleted moderator accounts. Exposure of this field to unprivileged callers may be restricted by PII/audit policies.

id.description: Unique identifier of the authenticated moderator.

username.description: Unique moderator username. Use for display and authentication lookups (no credential data included).

email.description: Moderator contact email. Included only for administrative contexts. Sensitive credential fields (password_hash) are NEVER exposed.

display_name.description: Optional human-friendly display name shown in UI and audit records. Null when not set.

created_at.description: Record creation timestamp in ISO 8601 UTC. Maps to discussion_board_moderator.created_at.

updated_at.description: Record last modification timestamp in ISO 8601 UTC. Maps to discussion_board_moderator.updated_at.

moderator.description: Optional moderator summary info for client-side display; excludes sensitive fields.

IDiscussionBoardModerator.IAuthorized.description: Response returned after successful moderator authentication or token refresh. Contains moderator id and authorization tokens; includes a moderator summary for convenience.

IDiscussionBoardModerator.ILogin.description: Moderator login request payload. The server validates credentials against discussion_board_moderator and creates a discussion_board_moderator_sessions row on success. Includes required session-context fields (href, referrer) which are recorded into discussion_board_moderator_sessions for audit and traceability. Do not include password_hash or other sensitive fields in this request.

usernameOrEmail.description: Moderator's username or email address used for authentication. Accepts either the account username or the verified email. Clients SHOULD trim whitespace and normalize case for email lookups (server may still perform case-insensitive lookup for emails).

password.description: Plain-text moderator password for verification. Transport must use TLS; do NOT expose this value in responses. Server MUST enforce password policy: minimum 12 characters and at least three of the following categories: uppercase, lowercase, number, symbol. The server MUST hash and compare against discussion_board_moderator.password_hash; never store or return plain-text passwords.

oneOf.description: Optional short-lived MFA code (TOTP or one-time numeric code). Provide when moderator account requires MFA. Pattern enforces a typical 6-digit code; servers may accept other formats but MUST validate server-side.
Explicit null when no MFA code is provided.

mfa_code.description: Optional MFA one-time code. Nullable to preserve backward compatibility.

ip.description: Optional client IP address observed for the login request. Provide null when unknown. This value is recorded in the created session for audit/context if present. Consider PII handling and redaction for unprivileged consumers.

href.description: Connection URL (current page URL). REQUIRED for moderator login and recorded into discussion_board_moderator_sessions.href for session context and audit. Must be a valid URI.

referrer.description: Referrer URL (previous page URL). REQUIRED for moderator login and recorded into discussion_board_moderator_sessions.referrer for session context and audit. Must be a valid URI.

IDiscussionBoardModerator.IRefresh.IToke.description: Refresh request payload variant using an opaque refresh token. Includes a discriminator property `type` with const value 'refresh_token'. Note: the authorization response (IAuthorizationToken) returns the issued refresh token under the property name `refresh`; client SDKs may normalize naming between request and response for developer ergonomics.

type.description: Discriminator for refresh-token variant with exact value 'refresh_token'. Use this exact literal when selecting this variant in a union.

refresh_token.description: Opaque refresh token previously issued to the moderator. The server validates this token and the associated session before issuing new access credentials. This request-side property intentionally uses the name `refresh_token` to make bearer intent explicit.

type.description: Discriminator for session-id variant with exact value 'session_id'.

session_id.description: Identifier of an existing moderator session (discussion_board_moderator_sessions.id). The server MUST validate the session exists, is not expired (expired_at), and belongs to an active moderator before issuing new credentials.

IDiscussionBoardModerator.IRefresh.ISess.description:
Refresh request payload variant using an existing moderator session identifier. Includes the discriminator property `type` with const value 'session_id'.

Notes: Implementations should treat this payload as a bearer of session-based refresh semantics. On success the server may extend the session expiry (sliding window), issue new access credentials, and optionally rotate refresh credentials. All refresh attempts MUST be logged to discussion_board_audit_logs for traceability.

IDiscussionBoardModerator.IRefresh.description:
Moderator refresh request. Accepts either a refresh_token or a session_id. This wrapper REQUIRES the discriminator property `type` to be present at the top-level. Use `type: "refresh_token"` with property `refresh_token` OR `type: "session_id"` with property `session_id`.

Security & business rules: The server MUST validate the provided bearer token or session id, ensure the referenced moderator account is active (discussion_board_moderator.deleted_at is null), verify session expiry (discussion_board_moderator_sessions.expired_at) when using a session, and audit the refresh event. Use the mapping to unambiguously select the correct variant for deserialization and code generation.

id.description: Unique identifier for the moderator. Maps to discussion_board_moderator.id.

username.description: Unique moderator username. Use for display and authentication lookups (no credential data included).

email.description: Moderator contact email. Included for administrative contexts and returned by this DTO. This field is non-nullable in the Prisma model and therefore is required in the response schema.

display_name.description: Optional human-friendly display name shown in UI and audit records. Null when not set.

created_at.description: Record creation timestamp in ISO 8601 UTC. Maps to discussion_board_moderator.created_at.

updated_at.description: Record last modification timestamp in ISO 8601 UTC. Maps to discussion_board_moderator.updated_at.

deleted_at.description: Soft-delete timestamp (discussion_board_moderator.deleted_at). Null indicates active record. Included to match Prisma model and enable admin/audit contexts to observe soft-delete state. Sensitive fields such as password_hash are intentionally excluded.

IDiscussionBoardModerator.description: Moderator entity returned by APIs. This schema is a safe, public-facing representation of a moderator and MUST NOT include sensitive fields such as password_hash. It exposes the moderator's email (required by the Prisma model) and temporal audit timestamps. x-autobe-prisma-schema links this DTO to the Prisma model discussion_board_moderator.

currentPassword.description: Current plain-text password for the authenticated moderator. The server MUST verify this against discussion_board_moderator.password_hash. Plain-text only; server is responsible for hashing and never persisting the plain value.

newPassword.description: New plain-text password. Must meet password policy: minimum 12 characters and at least three of the following categories: uppercase, lowercase, number, symbol. The server will hash and store the result in discussion_board_moderator.password_hash.

IDiscussionBoardModerator.IChangePasswor.description: Request DTO for the moderator change-password operation. The authenticated moderator's identity is taken from the JWT (operation.authorizationActor = "moderator"). Do NOT accept or include moderator id in this payload. On successful change, the implementation MUST revoke/invalidate existing moderator sessions (discussion_board_moderator_sessions) and record an audit entry (discussion_board_audit_logs).

IDiscussionBoardModerator.ISession.description: Moderator session record returned by moderator-facing session APIs. Maps to the Prisma model discussion_board_moderator_sessions. Returned only for the authenticated moderator (authorizationActor: 'moderator'). Access to this endpoint SHOULD be audited. Fields: id and moderatorId are UUIDs; createdAt/expiredAt use ISO 8601 date-time. Note: `ip` contains PII; implementations MAY return null to callers without audit/trace entitlement but the property is kept present to maintain a stable contract.

id.description: Unique session identifier. Maps to discussion_board_moderator_sessions.id.

moderatorId.description: Belonging moderator id. Maps to discussion_board_moderator_sessions.discussion_board_moderator_id. For this endpoint the value equals the authenticated moderator's id.

ip.description: Client IP address observed for the moderator session (discussion_board_moderator_sessions.ip). CONTAINS PII: implementations MAY redact this value (explicitly return null) for callers without audit/trace privileges; when unredacted this field is an IP string.

href.description: Connection URL (href) captured for the session. Maps to discussion_board_moderator_sessions.href (DB VarChar(80000)); may contain long URIs.

referrer.description: Referrer URL observed for the session. Maps to discussion_board_moderator_sessions.referrer.

createdAt.description: Session creation timestamp (ISO 8601 UTC). Maps to discussion_board_moderator_sessions.created_at and is set by the server at session creation.

expiredAt.description: Optional session expiry timestamp (ISO 8601 UTC). Maps to discussion_board_moderator_sessions.expired_at; null when the session is active or expiry is not set.

IDiscussionBoardModerator.ISessionsPage.description: Paginated list of moderator session summaries belonging to the authenticated moderator. Uses the canonical IPage.IPagination pagination wrapper and items of type IDiscussionBoardModerator.ISession (the session schema above). Returned sessions are limited to the authenticated moderator; servers MUST NOT return sessions belonging to other moderators.

pagination.description: Pagination information (current page, limit, total records, pages).

data.description: Array of session summary objects for the authenticated moderator.

IDiscussionBoardModerator.ISessionErased.description: Result object returned after attempting to revoke a moderator session. This payload is returned when the API responds with a success body (e.g., 200 OK) describing the revocation outcome. If the API is intended to return 204 No Content for successful revocation, the operation response should be updated to remove this schema and return 204 instead. `message` is nullable and should be used only for short human-facing notes (max 500 chars).

erased.description: Indicates whether the targeted session was successfully revoked. True on successful revocation.

id.description: Identifier of the session that was revoked (echoes the requested sessionId).

message.description: Optional short human-readable explanation for the result (nullable). Use for brief status/context; avoid including PII or detailed diagnostics.

notFoundOrForbidden.message: Session not found or not owned by caller

IDiscussionBoardCategory.IRequest.description: Pagination, filtering and sorting parameters for listing discussion board categories. By default listings exclude soft-deleted categories unless includeArchived is true. The server maps client-facing camelCase tokens to DB column names (for example: sort 'createdAt' -> created_at). The DTO provides both camelCase and snake_case aliases for compatibility with variants that expose Prisma-derived names.

search.description: Full-text search term applied to name and slug (partial match).

isActive.description: Optional camelCase filter: when true return only active categories. Provided for API parity with camelCase request shapes.

is_active.description: Snake_case alias for isActive retained for compatibility with Prisma-derived DTOs and admin clients. Server SHOULD accept either `isActive` or `is_active` and map both to the same DB predicate (discussion_board_categories.is_active).

createdFrom.description: Inclusive lower bound for created_at (ISO 8601 datetime). Use to filter categories created at or after this timestamp.

createdTo.description: Inclusive upper bound for created_at (ISO 8601 datetime). Use to filter categories created at or before this timestamp.

oneOf.description: Sort by created_at ascending.
Sort by created_at descending.
Sort by sort_order ascending.
Sort by sort_order descending.

sort.description: Sort order token. Server maps tokens to DB columns (e.g., 'sortOrder' -> sort_order). Use a leading '-' to indicate descending order.

includeArchived.description: When true, include soft-deleted (archived) categories (deleted_at not null) in results. Default behavior is false (exclude archived). Use only when the caller is allowed to view archived records.

IDiscussionBoardCategory.description: Discussion board category entity mapped to the Prisma model `discussion_board_categories`. Represents a primary organizational bucket for articles (for example: Economics, Policy). Properties mirror the database columns defined in the Prisma schema. Fields that are system-managed (id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at) are included to present the canonical persisted record.

id.description: Unique identifier of the category (Prisma: discussion_board_categories.id).

name.description: Human-readable category name used in listings and UI (Prisma: name). Must be unique.

slug.description: URL-friendly unique identifier for the category (Prisma: slug). Example: "economics". Uniqueness is enforced by the database (@@unique([slug])). Lower-case slug values are recommended.

description.description: Optional longer description explaining the category's scope and usage guidance (Prisma: description). Nullable.

is_active.description: Whether the category is active and available for assignment to new articles (Prisma: is_active).

sort_order.description: Optional integer used to order categories in curated lists; lower values appear first (Prisma: sort_order). Nullable.

created_at.description: Record creation timestamp (ISO 8601 UTC). The Prisma schema recommends a DB default such as now() to populate this value.

updated_at.description: Record last modification timestamp (ISO 8601 UTC). The Prisma schema recommends using @updatedAt or a DB trigger to keep this value current.

deleted_at.description: Soft-delete timestamp; null when active (Prisma: deleted_at). Presence indicates the category was soft-deleted and should not be offered for new article assignments.

IDiscussionBoardCategory.ICreate.description: Create DTO for discussion board category. Maps to the Prisma model `discussion_board_categories`. This request body is used by administrative create endpoints. System-managed fields (id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at) MUST NOT be provided by clients. The service will enforce uniqueness for `name` and `slug` and return 409 on conflicts.

slug.description: URL-friendly unique identifier (required). Example: "economics". Service validates uniqueness and recommends lowercase.

description.description: Optional longer description or usage guidance. Nullable.

is_active.description: Whether the category is active and assignable. If omitted the service MAY default this to true.

sort_order.description: Optional ordering integer used to order categories in curated lists. Lower values appear first. Nullable.

v0.name: Economics
v0.description: Articles and analysis related to macro- and micro-economics.

IDiscussionBoardCategory.IUpdate.description: Update DTO for discussion board category. Maps to the Prisma model `discussion_board_categories`. All properties are optional for partial updates. NOTE: The category `slug` is an immutable path identifier and MUST NOT be supplied in update payloads. The server updates `updated_at` on successful change.

name.description: Optional new human-readable category name. Must remain unique if provided (database enforces uniqueness). Recommended length: 3-200 characters. Server will trim whitespace and validate uniqueness before persisting.

description.description: Optional updated description. Provide a string to set or null to clear the description. Max recommended length: 2000 characters.

is_active.description: Optional activation flag controlling whether the category is assignable to new articles. When true the category appears in assignment UIs; when false it is hidden from new assignments but existing articles retain their category unless changed by an admin.

sort_order.description: Optional integer used to order categories in curated lists; lower values appear first. Provide null to remove explicit ordering and revert to default ordering behavior.

value.description: Updated category guidance: use for macroeconomic topics.

IDiscussionBoardTag.description: Tag entity representing a discussion_board_tags row. Maps directly to the Prisma model `discussion_board_tags`. Contains public-facing fields used for article labeling and discovery. Timestamps are server-managed and use ISO 8601 date-time format.

name.description: Human-readable tag name used in listings and UI (discussion_board_tags.name). Recommended length: 1-100 characters. Server enforces uniqueness for `name`.

slug.description: URL-friendly unique tag key (discussion_board_tags.slug). Recommended: lower-case, hyphen-separated (e.g., 'inflation'). The database enforces uniqueness; servers SHOULD normalize to lower-case for lookups when case-insensitive behavior is desired.

description.description: Optional longer description explaining the tag's purpose (discussion_board_tags.description). Provide null to clear. Max recommended length: 2000 characters.

is_active.description: Whether the tag is active and assignable (discussion_board_tags.is_active). Inactive tags should not be offered in tag selection UIs but remain on existing articles until changed.

sort_order.description: Optional integer used to order tags in curated lists; lower values appear first. Nullable when no explicit ordering is set.

created_at.description: Record creation timestamp in ISO 8601 UTC (discussion_board_tags.created_at). This field is server-managed and present in response DTOs.

updated_at.description: Record last modification timestamp in ISO 8601 UTC (discussion_board_tags.updated_at). Server-managed and updated on changes.

deleted_at.description: Soft-delete timestamp; null when active (discussion_board_tags.deleted_at). Presence indicates the tag has been archived/soft-deleted and public endpoints should exclude it unless includeArchived is requested by an authorized caller.

value.name: Inflation
value.description: Articles and analysis related to inflation and price dynamics.

page.description: Page number for pagination (1-based). Default is 1. Must be an integer >= 1.

limit.description: Number of items per page. Default is 20. Maximum 100.

search.description: Full-text search term applied to name, slug, and description using trigram/GIN indexes. Use simple words or phrases; complex queries may be rate-limited by server.

is_active.description: Optional filter by active state; true returns active tags, false returns inactive tags.

createdFrom.description: Inclusive lower bound for created_at (ISO 8601 datetime). Use to return tags created at or after this timestamp.

createdTo.description: Inclusive upper bound for created_at (ISO 8601 datetime). Use to return tags created at or before this timestamp.

oneOf.description: Sort option. Allowed tokens: 'createdAt','-createdAt','name','-name'. Use a leading '-' for descending order.

sort.description: Sort option. Allowed tokens: 'createdAt','-createdAt','name','-name'. Use a leading '-' for descending order.

includeArchived.description: When true, include soft-deleted (archived) tags (deleted_at != null) in results. Default false. NOTE: inclusion of archived rows may be restricted to privileged callers (moderator/admin) and is subject to RBAC; servers SHOULD ignore this flag for public callers.

IDiscussionBoardTag.IRequest.description: Request DTO for searching and paginating discussion_board_tags. All fields are optional; the server applies sensible defaults when omitted. Public callers receive only non-archived results by default.

IDiscussionBoardTag.ICreate.description: Create DTO for discussion_board_tags. Used by moderator or taxonomy-management actors to create new tags. Required fields: name and slug. System-managed fields (id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at) MUST NOT be provided by clients; the server populates those values. The server will set is_active = true when omitted.

name.description: Tag display name (required). Human-friendly label shown in UIs. Must be unique across tags; server enforces uniqueness and returns 409 Conflict on duplicate.

slug.description: URL-friendly unique tag key (required). Recommended lower-case, letters and digits with optional single hyphen/underscore separators (example: 'inflation', 'trade-policy'). Server SHOULD normalize to lower-case before persisting and will enforce uniqueness at the DB level (@@unique([slug])).

description.description: Optional longer description or guidance for tag usage. Nullable.

is_active.description: Whether the tag is active and assignable. When omitted the server will set is_active = true. This field is non-nullable in the Prisma model and the API documents the default behavior to avoid persistence errors.

sort_order.description: Optional integer used to order tags in curated lists; lower values appear first. Nullable in the Prisma schema.

v0.name: Economics
v0.description: Articles and analysis related to macro- and micro-economics.

IDiscussionBoardTag.IUpdate.description: Update DTO for discussion_board_tags. Allows modifying editable fields of an existing tag. The canonical slug is immutable and MUST NOT be included in update payloads (the service will return 400 if slug is present). Fields are optional; only provided fields will be updated. Calls must be recorded in moderation/audit logs by the server. This DTO maps to the Prisma model `discussion_board_tags` and preserves the model's nullability and types.

name.description: Optional new display name for the tag. The server MUST enforce uniqueness of `name` across tags and return 409 Conflict when the update would violate the database unique constraint. Trim and normalize whitespace as needed prior to uniqueness checks.

description.description: Optional longer description for the tag. Provide null to clear the description. Max length 1000 characters. The server SHOULD sanitize stored text to prevent XSS and remove control characters when rendering.

is_active.description: Optional activation flag. When omitted the existing `is_active` value is preserved. When provided, the server SHALL apply the new boolean value and record the change in audit logs for moderator actions.

IDiscussionBoardSetting.description: Runtime configuration entry mapping to the Prisma model `discussion_board_settings`. Represents a single key/value setting used for feature flags, thresholds, and other operational configuration. Fields map directly to persisted columns and are returned for administrative/moderator consumers. The `value` property is stored as a string; consumers interpret it according to the key's semantics (boolean, numeric, JSON, or text). Servers SHOULD validate and parse the stored string per known key expectations and reject semantically invalid values with 400. Soft-deleted entries (deleted_at != null) are treated as not found for standard reads unless an explicit administrative retrieval mode is used.

key.description: Global unique settings key (for example: 'moderation.auto_hide_report_threshold'). Use this key as the canonical business identifier for lookups and path parameters. The database enforces uniqueness on this column.

value.description:
Settings value stored as a string. Consumers interpret this string as boolean, number, JSON or text depending on key semantics. Common patterns:
- boolean: 'true' or 'false'
- integer/number: '5' or '0.75'
- JSON-encoded object: '{"enabled":true,"variant":"A"}'

Servers SHOULD validate and, where applicable, parse structured JSON values and enforce size limits to avoid excessively large values. When the key expects structured JSON the server SHOULD validate JSON shape and return 400 on parse/validation errors.

description.description: Optional human-friendly description explaining the purpose of the setting. Nullable when no description provided.

is_active.description: Whether the setting is active and should be considered by runtime code. For newly-created settings the server MAY default this to true unless otherwise specified.

created_at.description: Record creation timestamp (ISO 8601 UTC).

deleted_at.description: Soft-delete timestamp. When present (non-null) the record is considered archived and standard GET-by-key operations SHOULD return 404 Not Found unless an administrative retrieval mode is requested.

value.description: Toggle to enable the experimental editor UI
Number of unique reports within window required to auto-hide content

IDiscussionBoardSetting.IRequestItem.description:
Single entry in a batch settings update request. Clients must provide the existing `key` and the new `value`. `is_active` may be provided to toggle activation. This DTO intentionally excludes system-managed fields (id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at) and actor identifiers.

Behavioral notes:
- The server stores `value` as a string in the database; callers SHOULD serialize booleans, numbers, or structured JSON into strings according to key semantics (examples shown). 
- The server validates keys against the persistent catalogue of settings; unknown keys SHOULD result in a 4xx error unless the API explicitly allows creation of new keys (product decision). 
- Changes to settings MUST be audited. The operation applying this DTO SHOULD record who changed the setting and when.

key.description: Unique settings key to update. Must match an existing setting key (discussion_board_settings.key). Example keys: 'moderation.auto_hide_report_threshold', 'notifications.email.enabled'. Keys are case-sensitive as persisted. Allowed characters: letters, digits, dot (.), underscore (_) and hyphen (-).

value.description: New string value for the setting. Since the persisted column is a string, callers SHOULD serialize typed values into strings according to the key's semantics. Examples: 'true' (boolean true), '5' (number), '{"threshold":10}' (JSON object). The server will parse and validate the string and return a 400 with details when parsing fails or the value is semantically invalid for the named key.

is_active.description: Optional boolean to enable or disable the setting. If omitted, the server SHOULD leave the existing `is_active` state unchanged. When provided the server will set the persisted boolean accordingly.

IDiscussionBoardSetting.IRequest.description:
Batch update request for multiple DiscussionBoard settings. Contains an array of setting update entries. This request DTO does NOT accept system-managed fields (id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at) or actor identifiers; moderator identity is inferred from the authenticated session.

Behavioral notes:
- The server SHOULD apply the batch atomically when possible. If the server supports partial-apply it MUST document the semantics (which items succeeded/failed). The recommended default is transactional apply (all-or-nothing) with a clear 4xx error reporting invalid keys or value parse failures.
- Each change MUST be audited with moderator identity and a short reason/note when applicable.

settings.description: Array of settings to update. Each item must include the existing `key` and the new `value`. `is_active` is optional per item. The server SHOULD validate each key exists and validate `value` per key semantics before persisting changes.

batchExample.summary: Batch update example with mixed typed values (encoded as strings)

IDiscussionBoardSetting.ICreate.description: Create DTO for a runtime configuration entry. Maps to the Prisma model discussion_board_settings. Clients MUST provide the unique `key` and the `value` as strings. `description` and `is_active` are optional. The server will set `created_at`/`updated_at` and persist the record. The `key` is the immutable business identifier and uniqueness is enforced by the database; duplicate key attempts MUST return 409 Conflict. Authorized actor: moderator (privileged).

key.description: Unique business key for the setting (immutable). Examples: 'moderation.auto_hide_report_threshold', 'feature.enable_new_editor'. The server enforces uniqueness (DB @@unique([key])) and will return 409 on duplicate keys. Use stable, machine-friendly names (lowercase, dot-separated).

value.description: String representation of the setting value. Consumers interpret the string according to key semantics (boolean, number, JSON or text). For structured settings provide a JSON-encoded string (e.g., '{"threshold":10}'). The server MAY validate JSON shape for keys that expect structured content.

description.description: Optional human-friendly description explaining the setting's purpose. Nullable. Provide explicit null to clear existing description on update.

is_active.description: Optional flag indicating whether the setting is active. When omitted the server will default this to true for newly-created settings unless service policy dictates otherwise. The runtime system should ignore inactive settings.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.IRequest.description: Search and pagination request for DiscussionBoard articles. This DTO is used to express filters and pagination for listing/search endpoints. Note: Public callers must not set state to non-public values; server enforces visibility rules. The `is_pinned` filter aligns with the Prisma column discussion_board_articles.is_pinned.

IDiscussionBoardAttachment.description: Attachment metadata for an article attachment. Maps to Prisma model discussion_board_attachments for persisted fields. The schema includes storage_key and article_id (DB columns). Implementation guidance: servers SHOULD avoid exposing raw storage_key to unprivileged public callers and instead return signed `downloadUrl`. storage_key is included to reflect the persisted model and to satisfy upload/create flows that require it.

original_filename.description: Filename supplied by the uploader at time of upload.

storage_key.description: Object storage key or URI referencing the persisted file. This field maps to the DB column discussion_board_attachments.storage_key. Because this value is sensitive, implementations SHOULD return a signed downloadUrl to public callers and only return the raw storage_key to privileged/admin callers or internal APIs.

mime_type.description: MIME type reported for the file (e.g., image/jpeg, application/pdf).

is_image.description: Indicates whether the attachment is an image type (true) or not (false).

created_at.description: Timestamp when the attachment was uploaded (ISO 8601 UTC).

deleted_at.description: Soft-delete timestamp when the attachment was marked deleted. Null if not deleted.

uploader.description: Lightweight summary of the uploading member (discussion_board_member). Nullable when uploader was removed or upload was anonymous.

downloadUrl.description: Signed, time-limited download URL (CDN or storage proxy). Provided to authorized clients instead of exposing raw storage_key. The server must generate and expire this URL appropriately; quarantined attachments MUST NOT have usable downloadUrl for public callers.

cdnUrl.description: Optional CDN URL for the attachment when publicly available. Nullable when signed download URL or access restrictions apply.

IDiscussionBoardCategory.ISummary.description: Summary view of a category used in listings and article summaries. Maps to discussion_board_categories. Exposes essential, non-sensitive columns and includes optional metadata (description, sort_order, updated_at, deleted_at) derived from the Prisma model for richer admin/listing UX.

sort_order.description: Optional integer used to order categories in curated lists; lower values appear first (discussion_board_categories.sort_order). Nullable.

created_at.description: Record creation timestamp in ISO 8601 UTC (discussion_board_categories.created_at).

updated_at.description: Record last modification timestamp in ISO 8601 UTC (discussion_board_categories.updated_at). Nullable when unknown.

deleted_at.description: Soft-delete timestamp; null when active (discussion_board_categories.deleted_at). Presence indicates the category was soft-deleted and should not be offered for new article assignments.

IDiscussionBoardTag.ISummary.description: Summary view of a tag used in lists and article summaries. Maps to discussion_board_tags. Exposes essential, non-sensitive columns and includes optional metadata (description, updated_at, deleted_at) derived from the Prisma model for richer admin/listing UX.

description.description: Optional description or guidance for tag usage (discussion_board_tags.description). Nullable.

is_active.description: Whether the tag is active and assignable (discussion_board_tags.is_active).

created_at.description: Record creation timestamp in ISO 8601 UTC (discussion_board_tags.created_at).

updated_at.description: Record last modification timestamp in ISO 8601 UTC (discussion_board_tags.updated_at). Nullable when unknown.

deleted_at.description: Soft-delete timestamp; null when active (discussion_board_tags.deleted_at). Presence indicates the tag was soft-deleted and should not be offered for new assignments.

IDiscussionBoardComment.ISummary.description: Summary representation of a discussion-board comment intended for list and embedding contexts. Maps to the Prisma model `discussion_board_comments`. Note: this is a lightweight view — author may be null when the account was anonymized or removed; do not return sensitive session-level PII in this summary.

content.description: Comment text content. In summaries the content may be truncated by the server for display purposes.

articleId.description: Identifier of the parent article. Corresponds to discussion_board_comments.discussion_board_article_id.

parentCommentId.description: Optional parent comment id. Null for root-level comments or when the parent was removed.

author.description: Author summary derived from discussion_board_author_id. Nullable when the author account was anonymized or removed.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the comment was created (ISO 8601 UTC). Maps to discussion_board_comments.created_at.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the comment was last updated (ISO 8601 UTC). Null when never updated.

isHidden.description: Flag indicating whether the comment is hidden due to moderation or automated rules (discussion_board_comments.is_hidden).

IDiscussionBoardArticle.ISummary.description: Lightweight summary of an article for lists and search results. Maps to the Prisma model `discussion_board_articles`. This DTO exposes only non-sensitive, presentation-friendly fields. Fields that may be null (author, publishedAt, category) reflect Prisma nullability.

excerpt.description: Optional short excerpt or lead text derived from article content suitable for list display. Server may compute and provide this; nullable when not available.

author.description: Author summary derived from discussion_board_member_id. Nullable for anonymized/removed authors or system-created drafts.

isPinned.description: Whether the article is pinned in listings (discussion_board_articles.is_pinned).

publishedAt.description: Publication timestamp when the article was published to public listings (discussion_board_articles.published_at). Null for drafts.

createdAt.description: Article creation timestamp (discussion_board_articles.created_at).

updatedAt.description: Last update timestamp (discussion_board_articles.updated_at). Nullable when unchanged since creation.

category.description: Primary category summary for the article (nullable). Maps to discussion_board_articles.discussion_board_category_id.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.description: Detail representation of an article (discussion_board_articles) returned after attachment update operations. Belongs-to references use .ISummary types to avoid circular expansion. Note: `author` is nullable when the original author account was anonymized or removed; clients must handle null author gracefully (e.g., display '[deleted]'). `attachments` is always returned as an array (empty when no attachments).

content.description: Full article body content (maps to discussion_board_articles.content).

author.description: Author summary object (discussion_board_member). Nullable when the author account was anonymized or removed; clients must handle null author (e.g., display '[deleted]').

is_pinned.description: Whether the article is pinned in listings (maps to discussion_board_articles.is_pinned).

created_at.description: Creation timestamp of the article (ISO 8601 UTC). Maps to discussion_board_articles.created_at.

updated_at.description: Last update timestamp of the article (ISO 8601 UTC). Maps to discussion_board_articles.updated_at.

attachments.description: Ordered array of attachment summaries associated with the article. Server returns an empty array when no attachments exist. Uses the public attachment summary type to avoid exposing internal storage metadata in public responses.
